item.title: [巴士的報] Semien hits tiebreaking HR against old team and Baty adds pinch-hit slam as Mets beat Rangers 7-2
item.dc:creator: Bastillepost
item.description:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Marcus Semien hit a tiebreaking homer in the eighth inning against his former team and Brett Baty added a pinch-hit grand slam in the ninth as the New York Mets beat the Texas Rangers 7-2 on Wednesday night.
Rookie right-hander Nolan McLean (12-10) allowed two runs and three hits
item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Marcus Semien hit a tiebreaking homer in the eighth inning against his former team and Brett Baty added a pinch-hit grand slam in the ninth as the New York Mets beat the Texas Rangers 7-2 on Wednesday night.



























Rookie right-hander Nolan McLean (12-10) allowed two runs and three hits over seven innings for the last-place Mets (73-85), who have won both games in Texas since ex-interim manager Andy Green was given the full-time position Tuesday.









































The Rangers (78-80) have lost three consecutive games and trail first-place Houston by a half-game in the AL West, with the Astros playing later in Seattle. They own the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas if the teams finish with the same record.



























Semien, traded by the Rangers to the Mets last November for Brandon Nimmo, launched his 15th homer this season off All-Star closer Jacob Latz (3-4) to give New York a 3-2 lead. Semien’s first homer since Aug. 7 snapped an 0-for-13 slump.



























Latz entered with two on and one out in the seventh, the first time he’s appeared before the eighth inning since April 12.












The Mets took a 2-0 lead in the third when Juan Soto followed Francisco Lindor’s two-out single with his 27th home run off starter Cody Bradford. It was Soto’s sixth homer this year against left-handed pitching.



























After that, Soto was intentionally walked three times — twice with runners on first and second and a left-hander on the mound.












Texas tied the score at 2 in the fifth after McLean retired the Rangers’ first 12 batters. Nimmo, who spent 10 seasons with the Mets, led off with a sharp single to right field. He advanced to second on Ezequiel Duran’s groundout and scored on Jake Burger’s single. Evan Carter drove in the tying run when he beat out a potential double-play grounder.



























New York left the bases loaded in the fifth and seventh after Soto was intentionally walked. He was given another free pass with first base open and two outs in the ninth, but Bo Bichette then walked against Trevor Williams to load the bases before Baty went deep.



























Rookie LHP Zac Thornton (5-5, 3.40 ERA) starts the series finale Thursday afternoon as the Mets look for a three-game sweep. Texas hadn't announced a scheduled starter.












See AP’s full MLB coverage here















Texas Rangers' Jake Burger, left, celebrates scoring on an Evan Carter force out grounder during the fifth inning of a baseball game against the New York Mets, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/LM Otero)

















Texas Rangers left fielder Wyatt Langford jumps to catch a fly out against New York Mets' Francisco Alvarez during the second inning of a baseball game, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/LM Otero)

















New York Mets' Juan Soto runs the bases after hitting an two homer during the third inning of a baseball game against the Texas Rangers, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/LM Otero)

















Texas Rangers pitcher Jacob Latz looks on after giving up a home run to New York Mets' Marcus Semien during the eighth inning of a baseball game, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/LM Otero)

















New York Mets' Marcus Semien (10) is congratulated by third base coach Jacob Latz as Semien runs the bases on a solo home run during the eighth inning of a baseball game against the Texas Rangers, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/LM Otero)

















KANSAS CITY, Mo. (AP) — Maikel Garcia had three hits and three RBIs, including a tiebreaking, run-scoring double in the seventh inning, as the Kansas City Royals beat the White Sox 5-4 Wednesday night and delayed Chicago's bid for a postseason berth.












Chicago could have secured its first playoff berth since 2021 with a win over the Royals and a Texas loss to the New York Mets.












Instead, Garcia and the Royals played the role of spoiler.












Connor Thomas (2-1) struck out one and allowed one hit in two scoreless innings for the win. Steven Cruz struck out two in the ninth and earned his eighth save.












Kansas City had three straight singles to open the bottom of the first and Garcia drove in two runs with a single to right. Vinnie Pasquantino followed with a double that scored Garcia. Pasquantino made it 4-0, scoring on shortstop Colson Montgomery’s throwing error.












Chicago opener Bryan Hudson recorded just one out while facing five batters and allowing four runs, three earned.












The White Sox responded with five hits in the third inning — including Kyle Teel’s two-run single and RBI hits by Miguel Vargas and Munetaka Murakami — sending 10 batters to the plate and tying the score at 4.












In his final start of the season, Kansas City's Seth Lugo allowed four runs on seven hits, striking out three in 3 1/3 innings. His 200 hits allowed lead the American League and his 99 earned runs allowed rank second.












Carter Jensen had three singles for the Royals (68-90), who snapped a five-game skid.












Braden Montgomery had three singles as the White Sox (81-77) remained one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians (82-76), who lost 1-0 to Boston.












Hagen Smith (3-3), the fourth of five Chicago pitchers, allowed a pair of hits and one run in the seventh.












The White Sox have not named a starter for Thursday's series finale. Royals RHP Randy Dobnak (3-4, 3.08 ERA) gets the start.












See AP’s full MLB coverage here















Chicago White Sox's Kyle Teel dives to third to advance on an RBI single by Miguel Vargas during the third inning of a baseball game against the Kansas City Royals, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

















Chicago White Sox's Munetaka Murakami watches his RBI double during the third inning of a baseball game against the Kansas City Royals, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

















Kansas City Royals' Maikel Garcia runs home to score on an RBI single hit by Vinnie Pasquantino during the first inning of a baseball game against the Chicago White Sox, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

















Kansas City Royals starting pitcher Seth Lugo throws during the first inning of a baseball game against the Chicago White Sox, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

item.content:encoded:
Jarren Duran went 2-for-3 with a stolen base and a run scored off the bench on Wednesday against the Guardians.

Only in this game because Ceddanne Rafaela had to leave early with hamstring tightness, Duran was the spark plug that the Red Sox needed. He helped break a 0-0 tie with a lead-off single in the sixth, advanced to second on a groundout, then came around to score on a single by Andruw Monasterio. That lone run held up as the only scored in this game and Duran stole a base later on as well to give him 20 on the season. That plus his 20 home runs, .207 batting average, and .629 OPS give Duran one of the most disappointing 20-20 seasons of all time.

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA - Chris Sale ha completado una de las temporadas más impresionantes en la historia de los Bravos. Pero, para él, la única temporada que importa es la que le espera a él y a sus compañeros de equipo.
Sale parecía un hombre con una misión clara: logró 10 ponches y aseguró otra temporada de al menos 200 ponches durante la victoria por walk-off de los Bravos por 3-2 ante los Rojos en el Truist Park. El lanzador zurdo afrontó esta última apertura de la temporada regular con la misma agresividad que mostrará cuando llegue la postemporada la próxima semana.
Dado que Sale está programado para abrir el primer juego de la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Nacional contra los Padres el martes, llegó a este encuentro sabiendo que tal vez no lanzaría más de cinco entradas. Afortunadamente, dispuso de un poco más de tiempo al terminar el quinto episodio con 199 ponches en su cuenta.
Tras retirar al dominicano Elly De La Cruz con un elevado al inicio de la sexta entrada, Sale concluyó su labor de 97 lanzamientos ponchando a Sal Stewart, quien se quedó mirando el tercer strike cantado. El lanzamiento en cuenta de 3-2 parecía estar ligeramente hacia adentro, pero la decisión del árbitro principal, Derek Thomas, permitió que los Bravos y sus aficionados disfrutaran de un momento especial.
Aliviado por no tener que retirar a Sale antes de que alcanzara la cifra de 200 ponches, el manager de los Bravos, Walt Weiss, caminó hacia el montículo para relevarlo. Los jugadores del cuadro interior rodearon el montículo y el veterano lanzador se retiró entre una gran ovación, mientras sonaba a todo volumen el tema "Hard Workin’ Man" del dúo Brooks & Dunn por el sistema de sonido del estadio.
Sale se une a su ídolo, Randy Johnson, como los únicos lanzadores zurdos en la historia de MLB que han registrado nueve o más temporadas con al menos 200 ponches. Nolan Ryan (15), Johnson (13), Roger Clemens (12) y Tom Seaver (10) son los únicos lanzadores con más de nueve temporadas de este tipo.
Sale permitió un jonrón inicial al dominicano Juan Brito, pero luego mantuvo a los Rojos sin anotar carreras durante el resto de su actuación de cinco entradas y dos tercios. El zurdo de 37 años terminó la temporada regular con una efectividad de 2.16. Los únicos lanzadores de MLB que cumplen los requisitos y presentan mejores marcas son Jacob Misiorowski (1.86) y Cam Schlittler (1.94).
Greg Maddux (1.56 en 1994 y 1.63 en 1995), el dominicano Reynaldo López (1.99 en 2024) y Warren Spahn (2.10 en 1953) son los únicos otros lanzadores de los Bravos desde 1920 que han registrado una efectividad de 2.16 o inferior en al menos 25 aperturas durante una temporada.
Sale comenzó la temporada del 2024 pensando que sería la última de su carrera, y la terminó ganando el primer premio Cy Young de su trayectoria. Las lesiones lo habían limitado a 151 entradas lanzadas entre 2021 y 2023; sin embargo, ha seguido mejorando a lo largo de cada una de sus tres primeras temporadas con Atlanta.
¿Cuántos lanzadores han registrado una efectividad de 2.20 o menos en 25 o más aperturas a los 37 años de edad o más desde 1950? Sale se une a Justin Verlander (1.75 en 2022) y Roger Clemens (1.87 en 2005) como los únicos integrantes de este grupo. Tanto Clemens como Verlander acumularon 185 ponches durante esas temporadas.
Esta fue también apenas la 27ma ocasión en que un lanzador de 37 años o más registró 200 ponches en una temporada. Existe un denominador común entre muchos de los lanzadores más recientes que han logrado esta hazaña:
• Sale, 2026 Bravos
• Charlie Morton, 2022 Bravos
• Morton, 2021 Bravos
• R.A. Dickey, 2012 Mets
• John Smoltz, 2006 Bravos
Sin duda, la edad no ha mermado la potencia del brazo de Sale. Su recta de cuatro costuras promedió 97.8 mph durante su última apertura de la temporada regular. Esa cifra igualó el tercer promedio más alto que ha logrado con este lanzamiento en cualquier partido como abridor, una marca que había alcanzado por última vez en 2018. Realizó cuatro lanzamientos a 99.5 mph o más rápido.
"Es increíble lo que está haciendo en esta etapa de su carrera", comentó Weiss. "Diría que su velocidad es tan buena o mejor que en cualquier momento de su carrera como abridor, lo cual es asombroso. Dadas las lesiones que sufrió durante sus años en Boston y su regreso tras ellas, es realmente una maravilla. Sí, algo verdaderamente especial".

item.title: [Boston Herald] Sonny Gray’s scoreless start powers Red Sox to close win over Guardians
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox pulled off a 1-0 series-evening win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night, despite the ongoing dearth of situational hitting that has plagued them for the last two weeks and intermittently throughout the season.
Boston batters tallied 12 hits, but went 2 for 14 with runners in scoring position, and left 11 men on base in eight innings.
Fortunately for the home team, Sonny Gray was on form in his final start of the regular season. The veteran right-hander tossed six shutout innings, with four hits, one walk and three strikeouts.
Gray’s sixth scoreless start of at least six innings this year tied his single-season high first set in 2015 and matched in 2025. He is the first Red Sox pitcher to make at least six such starts in his age-36 season or older since Luis Tiant in 1977, and only the fourth in franchise history (also Cy Young, Lefty Grove).
“Just a really good pitcher,” manager Chad Tracy said of his starter. “The level of consistency for him from start to finish has been very fun to watch, and impressive.”
Though Gray’s pitch count sat at 77 (52 for strikes) after the sixth and the game remained scoreless, Tracy went to his bullpen. With Boston’s postseason ticket punched on Sunday, the short hook could suggest Gray is getting the ball for Game 1 of the Wild Card series on Tuesday.
Cleveland southpaw Foster Griffin was not nearly as adept at keeping the Red Sox off the diamond. He struck out seven and issued no walks, but yielded 10 hits in six innings of one-run ball.
Save for Jarren Duran’s leadoff single and Andruw Monasterio’s two-out RBI single in the sixth, the Red Sox bailed Griffin out every time. They were 2 for 11 RISP through his six innings. Their nine men left on base during Griffin’s start included multiple in four of the first five frames and bases-loaded in the third.
“Yeah, I mean, take the positives,” Tracy said of the offense. “I thought we swung the bat great. We actually got some hits today. … Between (the two-out hits) and the accumulation of hits and base runners throughout the game, I thought it was a pretty good offensive night. Obviously you’d like to score more, but we did take better plate appearances.”
Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman, Boston’s elite bullpen trio all season long, ensured the slim lead held until the end with a scoreless inning apiece. Tracy revealed postgame their appearances were “planned out, regardless of how the game went.”
“That was great,” Tracy said. “To be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
Duran, who replaced Ceddanne Rafaela in center field in the top of the third, led off the bottom of the eighth with a single. His subsequent steal of second made 2026 his second career season with 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases (also 2024). Duran, Mookie Betts and Jackie Jensen are the only players in franchise history with multiple 20-20 seasons.
Rafaela’s first game back from a 10-day stint on the injured list with a right quad strain began in energetic fashion. He recorded each of the first three outs, including a diving catch to rob Guardians hitter Steven Kwan of a leadoff single.
But after pulling up lame at first base on his own leadoff single in the bottom of the second, Rafaela ultimately left the game with right hamstring tightness when the inning turned over. Tracy announced postgame that Rafaela will undergo an MRI on Thursday.
“No, I think it’s more frustrating (than disappointing),” Tracy said of the Rafaela situation. “You want to see everybody get to that finish line healthy.
“So more just when you see it, you’re concerned, you know? So (we) don’t know where we’re at with it yet. Hopefully, it’s not a huge deal, but still, yeah, makes your heart jump a little bit, and we’ll see where he’s at.”
Cleveland threatened against Whitlock in an eighth inning that saw both teams run out of ABS challenges. No. 9 hitter Brayan Rocchio led off with a single, and Whitlock issued a one-out walk to third baseman José Ramírez before getting an inning-ending double play from designated hitter Chase DeLauter.
After the Red Sox stranded Duran in the bottom of the eighth, Chapman took the mound for the first time since Sept. 13. Boston’s All-Star closer was back in top form after being day-to-day with lat tightness. He struck out the side, Jo Adell, and pinch-hitters Angel Martínez and Angel Genao on 12 pitches.
The Red Sox are 85-73 with four games left to play. Wednesday marked Tracy’s first win since the interim tag was removed on Tuesday.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Sonny Gray, Red Sox shut out Guardians, who remain 1 up on White Sox

item.content:encoded:
Andruw Monasterio’s sixth-inning RBI single and Sonny Gray’s six shutout innings propelled the Boston Red Sox to a 1-0 win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night.
The Red Sox (85-73) managed the lone run on 12 hits, all singles. They went 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position and left eight men on base through five innings before Monasterio’s run-scoring, two-out knock off Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) broke the deadlock.
In the sixth, Jarren Duran (2-for-3) lined a leadoff single to left and moved to second on a groundout. He scored from second base on Monasterio’s knock, sliding ahead of left fielder Steven Kwan’s relay throw and catcher Patrick Bailey’s tag.
Gray (18-5) struck out three while allowing four hits and one walk to increase his American League-leading win total. Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman each threw a scoreless inning to finish off Boston’s 17th shutout victory of the season.
Chapman struck out the side in the ninth to log his 35th save as Boston snapped a three-game losing streak.
Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela returned from a 17-game injury absence caused by a right quad strain to record all three outs in the first, including a spectacular diving catch on Kwan, the leadoff hitter who still went 2-for-4 for Cleveland (82-76).
Griffin worked six frames, striking out seven and allowing one run on 10 hits and no walks.
The Guardians remained one game up on the White Sox (81-77) in the American League Central after Chicago lost 5-4 at Kansas City on Wednesday.
Rafaela hit a leadoff single in the second inning but appeared to be in pain after reaching first. He stayed in the game to run the bases and initially took his defensive position before Duran replaced him. The Red Sox announced that Rafaela was dealing with right hamstring tightness.
Rafaela’s defense helped Gray retire the first six men he faced. Bailey recorded Cleveland’s first hit with a leadoff single in the third, but a 6-3 double play ended the inning without any damage. Gray fanned a pair of Guardians to strand two to end the fourth.
After the lone run scored and Gray exited, Guerrero struck out three in the seventh after a leadoff walk. Whitlock worked around Brayan Rocchio’s leadoff single and Jose Ramirez’s one-out walk in the eighth, inducing an inning-ending double-play grounder from Chase DeLauter.
–Field Level Media

item.title: [abc7chicago.com] Chicago Cubs, White Sox on verge of making MLB postseason
item.dc:creator: DAVID BRANDT AP Baseball Writer

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox move Sunday's game and will play doubleheader against Cubs on Friday with storm expected
CHICAGO -- Major League Baseball's postseason is rapidly approaching.
The Chicago Cubs and White Sox are among teams who had a chance to clinch a playoff spot Wednesday evening, but they both lost their games.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is rolling into the postseason and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup on Wednesday after a stint on the injured list.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves have also clinched spots in the postseason. Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, a three-time AL MVP, is dealing with a right calf strain that will likely keep him out through at least the Wild Card Series.
While the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here's some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
Here's who can clinch a playoff spot Wednesday
In the American League, the Cleveland Guardians can qualify for the postseason with a win at Boston and a loss by either the Texas Rangers or Houston Astros.
The Chicago White Sox can cap a turnaround season and earn a spot in October with a win over the Kansas City Royals and a loss by the Rangers.
Over in the National League, the Chicago Cubs can clinch a playoff spot with a win over the Miami Marlins or a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Philadelphia Phillies can clinch a wild card if they beat the Milwaukee Brewers and either the San Diego Padres or D-backs lose.
The Padres can clinch a playoff spot with a win over the Dodgers and a loss by the D-backs.
AL Central and West are tight, other division winners are set
There's quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Guardians (82-75) have a narrow advantage over the White Sox (81-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-79) and Astros (78-79) are fighting for the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Cubs (87-70), Padres (87-70) and Phillies (87-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but will almost certainly make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is Arizona (83-74), which is four games back. Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker for home field over Philadelphia and San Diego, and the Phillies own the tiebreaker over the Padres after sweeping that season series 6-0.
MLB's major awards probably won't have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston's Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero has also had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has an outside shot at a Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .314 and his 41 homers are tied with Caminero, but his 102 RBIs are six back of Baltimore's Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati's Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit's Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB's postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 29. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
Wild Card Series: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.
The Red Sox are adjusting the schedule of their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs because of a significant storm that's expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to the Boston area.
The team said it was moving the Sunday afternoon game to Friday to create a split doubleheader. The first game is scheduled to begin at 1:05 p.m. EST. The originally scheduled 7:05 p.m. EST night game was moved up to 6:05.
The Red Sox said in a press release Wednesday that the change was made in consultation with Major League Baseball.
The Cubs are currently in a tight race for one of the NL's three wild-card spots.
There was no mention of a change to Saturday's game, which is slated for a 7:15 p.m. EST first pitch.
ABC7 Chicago contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA (AP) — Chris Sale struck out 10 and reached 200 Ks for the season, Mauricio Dubón delivered a winning RBI single in the 10th inning, and the Atlanta Braves defeated the Cincinnati Reds 3-2 on Wednesday night.
Matt Olson and Austin Riley hit solo homers for the Braves. Brent Suter (3-2) worked a scoreless 10th inning and earned the win.
Sale went 5 2/3 innings and was removed after recording his third strikeout of the game of Reds rookie Sal Stewart. The 37-year-old left-hander has reached 200 strikeouts nine times, which is the most of any pitcher since 2013. In his final start before the postseason, he allowed one run on four hits. Sale hit at least 99 mph on the radar gun on 12 of his 97 pitches.
Olson’s home run was his 41st of the season and tied the game at 1 in the sixth. Riley's homer tied the game at 2 in the seventh. Dubón was 2 for 4 with a walk and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.
Reds right fielder Juan Brito led off the game with a home run to center field off Sale. He went 2 for 4, including his third homer of the season.
Braves reliever Robert Suarez pitched for the first time since June 19 after being sidelined due to elbow inflammation. He pitched the seventh inning and gave up a leadoff triple to Matt McLain and a sacrifice fly to Will Banfield that gave the Reds a 2-1 lead. He threw 13 pitches.
Braves right fielder Ronald Acuña Jr. sat out after suffering a bone bruise when he fouled a ball off his shin in Tuesday's 4-0 loss to the Reds. Braves manager Walt Weiss said Acuña was asking to play and felt he could play right field Wednesday, but the Braves decided to be cautious with a postseason berth clinched.
Up next
Braves RHP Tyler Mahle (7-10, 3.81) will make his final start before the postseason against Reds RHP Brady Singer (6-15, 5.67) in the series finale Thursday.

item.title: [jaysjournal.com] Blue Jays officially bow out of playoff race with another lifeless offensive showing
item.dc:creator: Matthew Sookram
item.description: They were two outs away from winning the World Series. Two, measly, outs. Instead, they lost one of the most heartbreaking Game 7's in baseball history and they won't even get a shot at redemption in 2026. The Toronto Blue Jays were officially eliminated from playoff contention on Wednesday afternoon (Sept. 23) after losing a 4-2 ball game to the Orioles in Baltimore. Like much of the season, the Blue Jays offense was painful to watch. They managed ten hits against Baltimore pitching, but went 1
item.content:encoded:
They were two outs away from winning the World Series. Two, measly, outs. Instead, they lost one of the most heartbreaking Game 7's in baseball history and they won't even get a shot at redemption in 2026. The Toronto Blue Jays were officially eliminated from playoff contention on Wednesday afternoon (Sept. 23) after losing a 4-2 ball game to the Orioles in Baltimore.
Like much of the season, the Blue Jays offense was painful to watch. They managed ten hits against Baltimore pitching, but went 1-for-14 with Runners in Scoring Position. 42-year-old future Hall of Famer Max Scherzer battled valiantly over five innings, but gave up four runs on four hits and three walks while striking out seven.
One of the big differences? The Orioles hit a two-run home run in the fifth off the bat of Pete Alonso. It was one of just five hits in the ball game for Baltimore. Out of Toronto's ten hits, four of them went for extra bases, all doubles, but without the ability to get a ball to leave the yard, the Blue Jays were left empty handed once the Nathan Lukes struck out to end the ball game.
Blue Jays ugly habit of not cashing in prevails once again as team is officially eliminated from playoff contention
That was the fitting frustration of the afternoon, and really, of the entire season. The Blue Jays had plenty of opportunities, but once again failed to turn them into crooked numbers that could change a game. Ten hits should be enough to put real pressure on an opponent, especially with the season on the line. Instead, Toronto kept finding ways to leave runners stranded.
With runners in scoring position this season, the Blue Jays produced a 92 wRC+, which ranked 28th in MLB, along with a .313 on-base percentage that ranked 29th. For a team that spent parts of the summer trying to convince itself there was still a path back into the postseason picture, that simply was not good enough. The lack of finishing power was just as damaging. Toronto hit only 34 home runs with runners in scoring position, tied for 27th in the league.
Of the Blue Jays’ 149 home runs this season, 84 came with nobody on base, and their overall home run total ranked dead last in baseball, tied with the LA Angels and the Milwaukee Brewers. The Brewers are playoff bound and might just be one of the World Series favourites and they found a way to score with limited power - something the Blue Jays did not. In fact, the Brewers have scored 806 runs, which is the second most in MLB.
On the day their playoff hopes officially disappeared, the Blue Jays never got the big swing the needed - a microcosm of their season long issues.
The season is technically not over. The Blue Jays still have more baseball to play later today (Sept. 23) as they are set to finish the second game of this day-night doubleheader. Then they will head home to play the Cincinnati Reds for three more games. What will follow is one of the longest winters in recent Blue Jays memory where the Blue Jays’ front office will have to go back to the drawing board to figure out what didn’t work and how to correct it before 2027.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] There's one insane way Yankees could face Guardians over Red Sox in Wild Card Series
item.dc:creator: Adam Weinrib
item.description: After Carlos Rodón took care of the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday afternoon, I tweeted that the Yankees had locked in homefield in the Wild Card Series and, with it, guaranteed they would not go to Fenway Park this postseason. I spoke slightly too soon. The Yankees are officially cemented as the AL's No. 4 seed; that won't change, after the Rays took care of business in the nightcap and ended any faint AL East title hopes. But while the Boston Red Sox remain overwhelmingly likely to be headed to Yan
item.content:encoded:
After Carlos Rodón took care of the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday afternoon, I tweeted that the Yankees had locked in homefield in the Wild Card Series and, with it, guaranteed they would not go to Fenway Park this postseason. I spoke slightly too soon.
The Yankees are officially cemented as the AL's No. 4 seed; that won't change, after the Rays took care of business in the nightcap and ended any faint AL East title hopes. But while the Boston Red Sox remain overwhelmingly likely to be headed to Yankee Stadium next week, their struggles down the stretch have opened a very strange door. Given the respective schedules of the Red Sox, White Sox, and Guardians, you can almost see a world where Boston has to head to the other side of the bracket instead.
We're not telling you what and what not to root for, but it's always fun to see Boston lose and struggle to harness their momentum ahead of an October run. If the Guardians handle business at Fenway, then struggle against a Royals team that wants to play spoiler, all the White Sox have to do is take care of KC and the Rockies. The Red Sox's sloppy final series with the Cubs, that may end up rescheduled and weather-addled, could factor into this calculus, too.
Red Sox could sneak into an easier path and avoid the Yankees until theoretical ALCS
Of course, don't get too excited; if this were to happen, the Red Sox would face borderline-.500 teams in the Astros/Rangers to kick off their playoff run, followed by a tilt with the AL Central winner. They'd have an easier shot at the ALCS that way, avoiding the Yankees/Rays until the best-of-seven. That may actually be what they'd want.
All of this to say: What happened to the beautiful world we used to live in in the 1990s/2000s where there was only one Wild Card and division rivals couldn't face each other before the ALCS? We should be sitting back with a bowl of popcorn laughing at the Red Sox falling short after their summer surge and gearing up for a Yankees-Guardians ALDS. Instead, MLB decided to embrace the NFL model and let sub-.500 loser teams into the big dance. Shame.
The Yankees' final five games are now officially meaningless, unless you like watching exhibition baseball and crossing your fingers that nobody slips on wet grass. While unlikely, this potential seeding swap at least gives us something to watch for (other than some Pete Alonso porch jobs and a Josh Hart bobblehead during the final weekend).

item.dc:creator: DAN GELSTON
item.description: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Christian Yelich and Brice Turang hit solo home runs, and the Milwaukee Brewers delayed Philadelphia’s potential postseason clinch with a 4-1 win over the Phillies on Wednesday night. item.content:encoded:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Christian Yelich and Brice Turang hit solo home runs, and the Milwaukee Brewers delayed Philadelphia’s potential postseason clinch with a 4-1 win over the Phillies on Wednesday night.
The Phillies needed both a win over the Brewers and a loss later Wednesday night by either Arizona or San Diego to secure their fifth straight trip to the National League playoffs. The Phillies started their run with a trip to the World Series in 2022, reached the NL Championship Series the next season and are coming off consecutive NL East titles.
The Phillies have to settle for a wild-card berth this season and are likely to open the playoffs next week on the road. The Phillies, Chicago and San Diego hold the three NL wild cards headed into the final games of the season.
The Phillies went 0 for 12 with runners in scoring position against the Brewers and left 10 runners on base.
Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said ahead of the game the team was willing to wait at Citizens Bank Park until after the Padres game ended, if necessary, to celebrate. No need to hang around.
Aaron Nola (7-11) had turned around a miserable season and posted a 1.86 ERA over his last eight starts as the longest-tenured Phillie got the chance to clinch. With a playoff party looming, he instead surrendered Turang’s 20th homer of the season in the first inning and Yelich’s 12th of the year in the second.
The Phillies scored their only run in the second inning after loading the bases with no outs against Brewers starter Logan Henderson (11-3). Henderson allowed four hits and one run over five innings to help the NL Central champion Brewers win their 99th game of the season.
Trevor Megill worked a scoreless ninth for his 30th save.
William Contreras extended his hitting streak to 11 games with a two-run single in the third for a 4-1 lead.
Nola struck out eight in six innings.
Up next
The Brewers did not announce a starter for Thursday's game. The Phillies send RHP Andrew Painter (3-10, 5.59 ERA) to the mound.

item.content:encoded:
Las Grandes Ligas comienzan a llegar a su fin. Con octubre a la vuelta de la esquina, los equipos de la MLB arrancan el camino rumbo al sueño de la Serie Mundial, desafortunadamente, para algunos equipos significa el fin del camino, caso de ello el de los Toronto Blue Jays, quienes sorpresivamente quedaron fuera de los Playoffs de la Liga Americana.
Referentes de México fuera
Pese a ser uno de los mejores equipos el año pasado, los Azulejos de Toronto no lograron encontrar el ritmo durante la temporada, dejando una marca de 77-81 y quedando matemáticamente eliminado de su zona.
La novena que cuenta con mexicanos como referentes, tales como: Alejandro Kirk, Brandon Valenzuela y José Rodríguez, quedó fuera oficialmente luego de caer ante los Orioles en su Juego 3 y siendo barridos en la serie.
Toronto llegó a este tramo de la temporada con pocas posibilidades de mantenerse con vida en la pelea por un boleto a la Postemporada. La novena canadiense no logró repetir el protagonismo que tuvo durante la campaña anterior y terminó alejándose de los puestos que daban acceso a octubre.
Para los mexicanos, la eliminación significa también el final de su participación en la campaña. Alejandro Kirk volvió a ser una de las piezas mexicanas más reconocidas dentro de la organización, aunque sufrió una importante lesión a mitad de campaña, mientras que Brandon Valenzuela y José Rodríguez fueron poco más frecuentes.
De la Serie Mundial a quedar fuera
El contraste es importante para los Blue Jays, pues después de disputar la Serie Mundial en 2025, el equipo no consiguió mantenerse en la pelea por el campeonato durante esta temporada. La novena canadiense perdió terreno conforme avanzó el calendario y terminó sin posibilidades de regresar a la lucha por el título.
Ahora, Kirk, Valenzuela y Rodríguez deberán esperar al próximo año para volver a buscar un lugar en la Postemporada de las Grandes Ligas. Mientras tanto, Toronto tendrá que comenzar a planear una temporada baja en la que buscará recuperar el nivel mostrado el año pasado.

item.title: [chicago.suntimes.com] Alex Bregman ‘felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face,’ working to make quick return to Cubs

Bregman and the Cubs have said they’ve received relative “great news” since, in terms of a potential return, one that could come as soon as this weekend. item.content:encoded:
Trust me, you don’t want to be Alex Bregman right now.
“I felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face, pretty much,” the Cubs’ third baseman said Wednesday, three days after he took a foul ball to the face while standing on deck during a game in Cincinnati.
Bregman and the Cubs have said they’ve received relative “great news” since, in terms of a potential return, one that could come as soon as this weekend.
But while that would be a boost to the Cubs’ chances as they approach the most meaningful games of their season, he’s dealing with some significant aftereffects, with multiple facial fractures.
“The pain’s been fine,” Bregman said. “I guess I fractured something right by the nerve in my face, so the whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb. As soon as the swelling goes down, I’m sure I’ll feel the breaks a little bit more.
“But all in all, I’m super lucky that it hit where it hit. A lot of gratitude, because if it was a few centimeters higher, it could have been detrimental.”
And here’s some more body horror:
“There’s a lot of fluid in my face,” Bregman said. “If I move, the fluid moves. If I’m bouncing up and down, my face feels like it’s bouncing up and down.”
All that is to illustrate what Bregman’s dealing with. But being the lauded hard-worker he is, it’s little surprise that he’s champing at the bit to get back in the lineup.
“[Tuesday] was brutal. I wanted to play,” he said. “I hope [to play this weekend]. We’ll see. One step at a time. I don’t know. I’m going to try to get in there [Wednesday].”
That last line was a joke, in case you were wondering. Bregman still has a lot to test out to see how he feels and how realistic such a quick comeback is.
“He’s doing well. But we’ve got to take some steps here,” manager Craig Counsell said. “I’m excited how he feels, and he’s excited. But he still needs to feel some things. He hasn’t run around yet, and he’s got to do that. He’s got to know what it feels like.
“We’ve got to be careful, and we’ve got to go through the proper steps.”
Bummer of a bunt
Utility man Matt Shaw entered Wednesday with a .176 batting average in his last 18 games.
He got a chance to help produce a run in extra innings Tuesday, but he popped up a bunt attempt with two men on and nobody out in the 10th inning of an eventual 8-2 loss.
It’s a relative nit to pick from a game in which the Cubs went 1-for-18 with runners in scoring position, but with a lot on the line in the season’s final week, it could be among the moments that loom large.
“These are the moments you prepare for,” Shaw said. “I know that I’m going to have a situation again where I’m going to have to put a bunt down. We all know what the stakes are. All we can do is keep preparing for these moments.
“An experience like this is going to help the next time I’m in that situation, and that’s all you can walk away with.”
Palencia back?
Since allowing seven runs in his first five outings after a lengthy IL stint, righty reliever Daniel Palencia hasn’t allowed an earned run in seven straight appearances, helpful as the Cubs look for their bullpen to stabilize before the postseason begins.

item.content:encoded:
Ceddanne Rafaela’s first game back from the 10-day injured list (right quad strain) lasted all of two innings before the Red Sox removed him for seemingly precautionary reasons.
Boston’s Gold Glove center fielder caught all three outs in the top of the first, even laying out for a diving catch of Cleveland Guardians’ Steven Kwan’s leadoff line drive.
But when Rafaela singled to lead off the bottom of the second, he grimaced as he ran and seemed to pull up lame on first base. He leaned over briefly as he stood on the bag, prompting a visit from manager Chad Tracy and a team trainer. After a few minutes’ discussion and some test running down the first base line, they allowed Rafaela to remain in the game.
Rafaela appeared to run normally as he advanced to second when Caleb Durbin reached first on a fielding error by third baseman José Ramírez, and initially remained on the field after the Red Sox failed to score in the bottom of the second. But Jarren Duran replaced him in center before the top of the third began.
“Just saw him continuing to flex it,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy told ESPN’s Buster Olney moments later on the game broadcast. “That’s all. He seemed to have felt some cramping in the back there. When he went back out there, he kept flexing it, so we said, let’s go ahead and make the change.”
Red Sox media relations announced Rafaela left the game with “right hamstring tightness” two innings later.
The Red Sox already planned to monitor Rafaela’s workload in Wednesday’s game, as the end of the Triple-A season on Sunday meant he returned without playing in single a rehab game.
“You guys know, every ball that gets hit up in the air in his direction, he thinks he can catch it,” Tracy said pregame. “So if you have a very normal, easy game flow, I think he’d be just fine. If you have a game flow where he tracks down seven balls in the gap and hits two doubles, you might say that’s enough.
“We’ll be very reactive to what the game is requiring of him and do our best to make sure we keep him in a good spot.”
Rafaela’s departure had consequences for the Red Sox almost immediately. They loaded the bases in the bottom of the third on back-to-back singles by Roman Anthony and Nick Sogard, and a two-out single by Adley Rutschman. Duran, batting in Rafaela’s No. 6 spot in the order, struck out swinging to end the inning.

item.title: [Fox News] Blue Jays' Vladimir Guerrero Jr. says his $500M contract was for past performance – not future results
item.dc:creator: Scott Thompson
item.description: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has four games left before he can put his 2026 Toronto Blue Jays season behind him. Guerrero, the six-time All-Star who signed the third highest-paid extension in MLB history in April 2025 at $500 million, has hit just nine home runs and slugged .359 to date for a career-low .695 OPS to date. The Blue Jays, winners of the American League pennant this past season, where Guerrero was a major factor in reaching the World Series, were mathematically eliminated from this year’s
item.content:encoded:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has four games left before he can put his 2026 Toronto Blue Jays season behind him.
Guerrero, the six-time All-Star who signed the third highest-paid extension in MLB history in April 2025 at $500 million, has hit just nine home runs and slugged .359 to date for a career-low .695 OPS to date.
The Blue Jays, winners of the American League pennant this past season, where Guerrero was a major factor in reaching the World Series, were mathematically eliminated from this year’s postseason race as they hold a 77-81 record entering Wednesday.
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
For a player that is worth so much, especially financially, to an organization’s success, Guerrero’s down year has led to some vitriol from the Blue Jays’ fan base. And that’s likely to continue after hearing recent comments from the star infielder.
Guerrero, 27, sat down with Telemicro News recently, where he discussed his struggles at the plate this season, and how it reflects on his contract extension.
His comments were, well, interesting.
"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I’m going to do," Guerrero said, as translated by MLB reporter Héctor Gómez. "I understand why the fans believe it’s the other way around. Sometimes, I think that way, too, like, ‘Oh, they give me this money, and I’m not doing enough,’ but you know I try my best, and I’m working hard.
"The fans, I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you. But when you are not at your best, not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."
After catching heat from Blue Jays fans, Guerrero was approached about the viral quotes, which he responded to.
"That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year," Guerrero said, via MLB.com. "I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason. I said I felt – that it’s my personal opinion – that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.
"To the fans, I’ve never stopped working very hard. I am going to go into the offseason again to prepare myself the best I can. Physically, mentally, everything that I have like I always do for my team and my teammates."
In Guerrero’s defense, that is technically what the Blue Jays did when they dished out his 14-year, $500 million extension, which is only behind Shohei Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Juan Soto’s 15-year, $765 million deal with the New York Mets. The franchise paid Guerrero for what he did from his debut in 2019 up to a fantastic 2025 campaign, where he belted eight homers and hit .397 across 18 postseason games.
But these comments show that Guerrero mustn’t be aware of what putting pen to money-filled paper meant in April 2025. No longer is it time in any sport, let alone Major League Baseball, where contracts are dished out based solely on past performance. It’s looking ahead to the future, where those past performances are expected to continue through a much-more lucrative deal.
MLB franchises sign players to contracts based on the market, and that market is justified by how the player will perform for them later on, while obviously looking at the track record in the past.
With any investment, those dishing out the big bucks want a return.
So, in a season where the home run total for a slugger is less than double digits – he still has time to at least get to 10 – and a career-low WAR (albeit the 2020 COVID-shortened campaign) has been accumulated, the Blue Jays and its fan base have every right to be disappointed. Yes, Guerrero was a major reason why Toronto reached the World Series in 2025, but the team and its fans are also allowed to voice displeasure with not just a down year – a career-worst performance in various metrics.
Would the Mets have dished out the highest-paying contract in league history if they didn’t expect Soto to continue performing at his superstar pace? No.
Would the Dodgers have agreed to give Ohtani $700 million, with heavy deferrals, might we add, to pay him for years without helping them reach their World Series goals? No.
From Mike Trout, to Mookie Betts, to Aaron Judge and the list goes on, every franchise wants to see a player they sign, especially for nine figures, to pay dividends. That’s the reality of the situation, whether Guerrero wants to view his deal as what he’s done in the past.
This is just one season, but Guerrero’s outlook needs to change just as much as his production moving forward on the remaining 13 years of his deal.

item.title: [fansided.com] Alex Bregman doesn't look like a guy ready to play a Cubs Wild Card series game
item.dc:creator: Chris Landers
item.description: Chicago Cubs fans around the country breathed a sigh of relief on Tuesday, when manager Craig Counsell sure made it sound like the team didn't expect Alex Bregman's ugly facial fracture to keep him out of the team's postseason lineup. In fact, Counsell went as far as to say the third baseman could be back in Chicago's lineup as early as this weekend. Just 24 hours later, though ... well, let's just say we have our doubts. Wednesday afternoon brought an interview with the man himself, and while B
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs fans around the country breathed a sigh of relief on Tuesday, when manager Craig Counsell sure made it sound like the team didn't expect Alex Bregman's ugly facial fracture to keep him out of the team's postseason lineup. In fact, Counsell went as far as to say the third baseman could be back in Chicago's lineup as early as this weekend.
Just 24 hours later, though ... well, let's just say we have our doubts. Wednesday afternoon brought an interview with the man himself, and while Bregman is grinning and bearing it as best he can, it's hard not to read between the lines here and wonder how exactly he'll be ready to play playoff baseball in a matter of days.
Bregman spoke to ESPN's Jesse Rogers prior to the Cubs' game against Miami, describing the fracture as "something by the nerve of my face" — adding that, as the swelling goes down, the actual fractures have become more and more painful. He did say that the pain was "fine," but, well, that's exactly what you'd expect someone of Bregman's track record to say. In reality, you need to see pretty well to hit a baseball, and even if Bregman does insist on toughing it out in October, you have to wonder what version of him Chicago will be getting.
Cubs fans probably shouldn't get their hopes up after Alex Bregman's latest injury update
From the "never a thing you want to hear an athlete say" department, Bregman also told Rogers that fluid build-up in his face is affecting him.
In a word: yikes. Again, Bregman is as tough a player as there is in the league, and he'll no doubt do everything in his power to be in the lineup when the Cubs kick off their Wild Card series (opponent TBD) next Tuesday. And to be sure, his face already visually looks a whole lot better than it did just 48 hours or so ago; give it another few days, and the swelling and bruising should subside even more.
All of which fails to reckon with the fact that Bregman has a broken bone in his face. Not just in his face, but awfully close to his left eye, the one closest to the pitcher as he steps in the box as a right-handed hitter. Less swelling is still some swelling, and there's still the pain — and, apparently, the fluids — to worry about. It seems almost unfair to expect Bregman to hit at anything like his usual level if he's having a hard time focusing on the baseball, and that should have the Cubs thinking long and hard about whether he belongs in the lineup.
Projected Cubs lineup if Alex Bregman misses Wild Card series
Of course, it's easy for me to say, and much tougher for Craig Counsell to actually execute. Not only is Bregman a veteran leader with a great deal of latitude, but his absence would leave a notable hole in the Cubs lineup.
| Player | Position |
|---|---|
| Pete Crow-Armstrong | CF |
| Seiya Suzuki | RF |
| Michael Busch | 1B |
| Ian Happ | LF |
| Nico Hoerner | 2B |
| Michael Conforto | DH |
| Dansby Swanson | SS |
| Pedro Ramirez | 3B |
| Carson Kelly | C |
Pedro Ramirez and Matt Shaw are both exciting, versatile young players, but installing them as an every-day third baseman for a playoff series feels like asking a lot. Both are just league-average hitters, and because of Bregman's iron-man tendencies, neither has a ton of third-base experience this year (though Shaw played there a bunch last season).
Chicago does have plenty of firepower around them, in the form of pending NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong, Seiya Suzuki, Michael Busch and others. But Bregman has been scorching hot for pretty much the entire second half, and losing his bat would be a devastating blow to a lineup that would suddenly start to look pretty top-heavy — especially with Dansby Swanson just making his way back from an oblique injury.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Can Padres' Manny Machado Earn Elusive World Series Title?
item.dc:creator: Chris Traczek
item.description: San Diego Padres third baseman Manny Machado is one of the most accomplished players of this generation, but will he be able to add a World Series title to his star-studded resume? Bryce Harper. Aaron Judge. Jacob deGrom. Tarik Skubal. Besides being certifiable MLB royalty, what do these players have in common? Despite collectively owning a number of Most Valuable Player and Cy Young Awards, and making a total of 20 playoff appearances over 46 combined seasons, none of them has been able to part
item.content:encoded:
San Diego Padres third baseman Manny Machado is one of the most accomplished players of this generation, but will he be able to add a World Series title to his star-studded resume?
Bryce Harper. Aaron Judge. Jacob deGrom. Tarik Skubal. Besides being certifiable MLB royalty, what do these players have in common? Despite collectively owning a number of Most Valuable Player and Cy Young Awards, and making a total of 20 playoff appearances over 46 combined seasons, none of them has been able to participate in that final champagne shower of the season, emblematic of the World Series champion.
The list also included third baseman Manny Machado of the San Diego Padres, who, according to the writer, "has been one of the best third basemen in the game for more than a decade," but aside from a 2018 deadline-day trade that sent him from the Baltimore Orioles to the Los Angeles Dodgers, who would lose that year's World Series to the Boston Red Sox, Machado has not otherwise appeared on the game's biggest stage, let alone won the ultimate title.
Still, it's safe to say that Machado has presided over the most successful period in the franchise's history. Since Machado signed with the Padres as a free agent before the 2019 season after 6-1/2 years with the Orioles and two months with the Dodgers, San Diego has made the playoffs four times (2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025).
The Padres also stand on the verge of qualifying again this season, which they can do with a win Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers and a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks to the Colorado Rockies. Should they earn an NL wild-card spot, it would be the first time San Diego has made the playoffs three seasons in a row. Not bad for a franchise that made the playoffs a grand total of five times in its 50 years of existence before Machado's arrival.
Machado's contribution to this growing history of success comes in the form of being one of the sport's most reliable players. In his 15th season overall and eighth with the Padres, Machado has been a model of consistency. He's been an All-Star seven times, is a three-time Silver Slugger winner, two-time Gold Glove recipient, has finished in the top 10 in MVP voting five times and compiled a 63.4 career WAR.
Even with all those honors, Machado's most significant "ability" may be his "availability." The only time he's missed any significant time with injury was during his second full season in Baltimore when he appeared in 82 games. Since joining San Diego, Machado has appeared in less than 150 games only once, when he played 138 in 2023, and he even appeared in all 60 games during the COVID-shortened 2020 season.
This year, he's played in 153 of San Diego's 157 games as of Wednesday and, after a stuttering start to the season (.182 average and .616 OPS through May 20), Machado has looked more Manny-like in the ensuing four months. As of Wednesday, he has 28 home runs with 84 RBIs, both of which are within career norms, though his average and OPS (.218 and .710, respectively) are career lows and his 139 strikeouts are a career high.
That being said, with 2,193 hits at the age of 33, Machado is the one active player "with the best chance of reaching 3,000 hits," according to a July 2025 report from The Athletic via The Sporting News. A similar report from MLB.com, also from July 2025, noted that with more than 2,000 hits and 350 home runs at the time, Machado was the 12th player in MLB history to reach those milestones in their age-32 season or earlier. The list includes Hall of Famers Hank Aaron, Lou Gehrig, Mickey Mantle, Willie Mays and Frank Robinson, and contemporaries Miguel Cabrera, Albert Pujols and Alex Rodriguez.
With continued good health and a contract that runs through the 2033 season, Machado will have ample opportunity to join the 3,000-hit/500-HR club, an exclusive group that includes just seven members: Aaron, Mays, Cabrera, Pujols, Rodriguez, Eddie Murray and Rafael Palmeiro.
But that's a discussion for another day. Of more immediate concern, do Machado and the Padres have what it takes to qualify for the playoffs and then make that magical run to a World Series championship? If the playoffs started Wednesday night, they'd travel to meet the Atlanta Braves in the three-game wild-card round. A win there would send them to Los Angeles to take on the Dodgers. Winning that series would match them in the NLCS against one of the Milwaukee Brewers, Chicago Cubs or Philadelphia Phillies. The likeliest World Series opponents would be the Tampa Bay Rays or New York Yankees.
This San Diego squad has definitely been built with a deep playoff run in mind. Michael King, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray and Nick Pivetta headline a solid rotation with the red-hot Fernando Tatis Jr. and Jackson Merrill pacing an offense that has helped the Padres win 13 or their past 15 games going into Wednesday night. The real key to postseason success lies in a shutdown bullpen led by Mason Miller, Adrian Morejon and Bradgley Rodriguez, who has been predicted to be a surprise postseason star.
And don't expect Manny Machado, who has been a foundational piece of this franchise for seven seasons, to be solely along for the ride as the Padres chase World Series glory.

item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE (AP) — The Toronto Blue Jays put right-hander Dylan Cease on the 15-day injured list with shoulder inflammation, ending his 2026 season.
The move came between games of Wednesday's doubleheader at Baltimore, after the Blue Jays dropped the opener and were eliminated from postseason contention. Cease went 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA this season, his first with Toronto.
Cease signed a $210 million, seven-year contract to join Toronto after he spent his first seven seasons with the Chicago White Sox and San Diego Padres. He made 29 starts this year. The last one was Friday, when he walked six batters and was replaced in the third inning.

item.title: [930 WFMD Free Talk] Sonny Gray and the Boston Red Sox host Cleveland Guardians in a potential MLB playoffs preview
item.dc:creator: Latest; Breaking News
item.description: The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team. item.content:encoded:
The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team.
Tonight, I’m going for a game that we could potentially see in the playoffs as the Guardians take on the Red Sox.
The Guardians are currently the owners of the top spot in the American League Central. As seems to be the case for Cleveland every season, they saved their best baseball for the end of the season. They’ve won six straight games, but they are only one game ahead of the White Sox, who have also won three straight games. The good news for both of them is that, as long as they both are winning games, they can both make the postseason. The magic number for the Guardians to make the playoffs is down to one.
Giving them a great chance today is the arm they acquired at the trade deadline, Foster Griffin. For the season, Griffin is 15-5 with a 3.67 ERA and a 1.19 WHIP. Griffin, overall, has been a nice addition to the team. He has two starts that were a little bit of a disaster, going four innings against the Mets and allowing five earned in his debut with the Guardians.
The Baltimore Orioles also knocked him around for eight runs in 2.1 innings. His other six starts saw him going for 22 innings and allow just 11 runs. He has never faced the Red Sox, so he could have them off balance the first time through the lineup.
The Boston Red Sox are one of those teams that are likely brimming with confidence. After a disaster of a start to their season, they pivoted and became one of the hottest teams in baseball right before the All-Star Break. They continue to be a streaky team, but the majority of their streaks have seen them winning games instead of losing them. They are still just an average team at Fenway with a 38-38 record for the season. It is almost hard to believe given how good they’ve been, but getting to .500 is impressive because of how bad they were early in the year.
The Red Sox are sending the one guy who was dominant at home all year, Sonny Gray. For the season, Sonny Gray is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA and a 1.16 WHIP. He should be in the running for the Cy Young Award, even though he won’t win over Cam Schlittler. He’s been solid in September, going 19.1 innings and allowing a total of six earned runs. He faced the Guardians earlier this season and allowed just one earned run over six innings in a 9-1 win for the Red Sox.
It wasn’t just that one game against the Guardians that Gray has excelled in. He has been great against them for years, holding hitters to a .208 batting average over 130 at-bats. Although the Red Sox don’t really “need” this game to solidify their Wild Card spot, they still should look to win. Gray has been dominant for them, and they’ve been very successful in his outings this year. I’m backing the Red Sox here and I also think they probably cover the -1.5 run line. I also would be surprised to see this game go under 6.5 runs. I’ll play all three bets.
For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

item.title: [southsideshowdown.com] White Sox' Miguel Vargas might've somehow snuck his way into AL MVP finalist conversation
item.dc:creator: Noah Phalen
item.description: There’s very little doubt who the MVP of the Chicago White Sox has been in 2026. After posting a .104 batting average in 42 games with the White Sox in 2024, very few people envisioned Miguel Vargas becoming the type of player he is now in just two years. In what feels like no time, Vargas has turned himself from a failed top prospect, to a serviceable starter, to one of MLB’s superstars. His incredible performance landed him a trip to Philadelphia for the All-Star game this summer, and it could
item.content:encoded:
There’s very little doubt who the MVP of the Chicago White Sox has been in 2026. After posting a .104 batting average in 42 games with the White Sox in 2024, very few people envisioned Miguel Vargas becoming the type of player he is now in just two years. In what feels like no time, Vargas has turned himself from a failed top prospect, to a serviceable starter, to one of MLB’s superstars. His incredible performance landed him a trip to Philadelphia for the All-Star game this summer, and it could soon land him a nomination for MLB’s most prestigious award: the MVP.
With just five games to play, the AL MVP award seems just about decided. Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has been the favorite for the majority of the season, and it’s easy to see why. In 153 games for Houston, Alvarez has slashed .314/.431/.601 with a 1.032 OPS and an AL-leading 41 home runs. Alvarez is one of the game’s most dangerous hitters and has had an impressive season from start to finish. His 6.5 fWAR is second in the American League, and as a primary DH, is completely driven by his offense. Above Alvarez is only Bobby Witt Jr, who continues to post impressive numbers despite a down year by his standards.
Immediately behind Alvarez is Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, the favorite for the AL Cy Young Award. Behind him is former White Sox ace Dylan Cease, who has excelled in his first year in Toronto. Next up? Miguel Vargas. His 5.2 fWAR ranks third among AL position players. While not impossible, it’s pretty rare that a pitcher ends up winning the MVP award. The Cy Young award essentially functions as the MVP for pitchers, so it’s very possible that Schlittler and Cease don’t become MVP finalists. That could leave Vargas next up on the list.
Miguel Vargas' underlying metrics support his excellent season
FWAR isn’t the definitive stat when it comes to a player’s value, but it’s typically a pretty good summary of a player’s offensive and defensive contributions. In 155 games this season, Vargas is slashing .251/.363/.481 with an OPS of .844 and 33 home runs, more than doubling his career high of 16 set in 2025. He’s also turned himself into a genuine threat on the bases, and his 20 steals leads the team. Vargas has elite totals in his xwOBA, xSLG, Barrel%, Sweet-Spot %, and has elite chase and walk rates, giving every indication that his breakout is real and not simply a run of good luck. If there’s any area he needs to improve, it’s his defense, but Vargas has been one of the best hitters in the American League this season.
Should Vargas be a finalist for the MVP Award, I wouldn’t expect him to win it. I wouldn’t even necessarily expect him to finish second. Alvarez is the overwhelming favorite to win the award, and Rays third-baseman Junior Caminero is the best player on the AL’s best team, giving him an edge as well. But the fact that Vargas may even be among the leaders is remarkable given the state of his career just two years ago.
Miguel Vargas isn’t just the best player on the White Sox and a building block of what they believe is an excellent young core, he’s the type of player and leader that can be the face of a franchise for many years to come. Hopefully, the writers recognize him as the backbone of MLB’s most remarkable story and reward him accordingly.

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Pete Alonso gets MVP push after helping Orioles eliminate Blue Jays
item.dc:creator: Kevin Henry
item.description: BALTIMORE — Wednesday afternoon's game between the Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards had more of a spring training environment than two teams battling to stay alive in the American League postseason race deserved. A postponement of Tuesday night's clash between the AL East rivals forced a split doubleheader on Wednesday, and the sparse crowd of 10,562 in Baltimore reflected the reality of a Wednesday matinee. However, those in attendance were treated to more
item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE — Wednesday afternoon's game between the Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards had more of a spring training environment than two teams battling to stay alive in the American League postseason race deserved.
A postponement of Tuesday night's clash between the AL East rivals forced a split doubleheader on Wednesday, and the sparse crowd of 10,562 in Baltimore reflected the reality of a Wednesday matinee.
However, those in attendance were treated to more history from Pete Alonso in what has been a magical season in Charm City.
Alonso smashed a two-run homer, his 41st of the season, to pace Baltimore to a 4-2 win and stay alive for the postseason. His home run off Toronto's Max Scherzer pushed Alonso into a tie for first in the AL with Houston's Yordan Alvarez and Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero. He also ended the afternoon as the AL's leader in RBI with 110.
Pete Alonso extends the @Orioles lead with a 2-run shot ❄️ pic.twitter.com/4gBdpOtdDu
— MLB (@MLB) September 23, 2026
All of those stats and all of the things that Alonso has meant to the Orioles this season makes the veteran first baseman a strong candidate for the AL Most Valuable Player Award, said teammate Chris Bassitt.
"Pete deserves MVP votes, and he deserves them every single year. That's just the reality," Bassitt said after earning his ninth victory of the season on Wednesday afternoon. "He's one of the most underappreciated players in our game. He's easily in the top three hitters every single year."
Each of Alonso's last six hits have been home runs, becoming the first Oriole to accomplish that since Mark Trumbo hit seven home runs between Aug. 11-22, 2016.
"He's not having a crazy historical year for his standards. It's just Pete being Pete," Bassitt said. "I think Pete has held the standard of what he's done for years, and I think people are not only realizing 'Holy s--t, this guy's really good' but that he's always been really, really good."
Just how good has Alonso been? The power numbers tell the story.
Most home runs in first 8 MLB seasons:
Ralph Kiner: 329
Albert Pujols: 319
Pete Alonso: 305 https://t.co/5eKyUxKvUJ
While Alonso's blast in Wednesday afternoon's win kept the Orioles mathematically alive for the postseason, Orioles manager Craig Albernaz wanted to make sure Bassitt's 90-pitch performance wasn't overlooked.
"It was definitely a gritty outing," Albernaz said of Bassitt scattering seven hits over 5.0-plus innings but allowing just two runs. "He made pitches when he had to. He had more in the tank but he did his job today. He gave us a chance to win and threw a lot of strikes."

item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is thankful he’s not a little shorter.
Sporting a discolored left eye after being struck by a foul ball in the on-deck circle Sunday, the three-time All-Star said it could’ve been worse.
“Super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn’t a few centimeters higher,” he said before Wednesday night’s game against Miami.
The ball, off the bat of teammate Michael Busch n Cincinnati, caused several facial fractures.
With the postseason approaching, the Cubs are glad the injury won’t require a stint on the injured list.
Bregman said he’ll likely start shagging ground balls in a day or so and will be trying out new styles of helmets to protect the eye.
“The whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb,” he said.
The Cubs can clinch an NL wild-card berth with a win Wednesday night or an Arizona loss.
“He’s still got significant swelling in his face and his eye that needs to improve,” Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Tuesday. “But all things considered, he’s in a good place.”
Bregman was on deck in the fourth inning of a 9-1 win at Cincinnati when he was hit on the left side of his face by Busch’s check-swing foul. Bregman immediately jogged toward the Cubs’ dugout and covered his face before going back to the clubhouse with an athletic trainer.
“When everything was going down on Sunday afternoon, I think that we all thought the worst case might be a possibility,” president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer said Tuesday. “And all the news since then has been really good. He’s had a lot of different doctor’s appointments, and they’ve been positive. And I think we have to take it one step at a time.”
Bregman is batting .262 with 26 homers and 89 RBIs in 153 games during his first season with Chicago. He signed a $175 million, five-year contract with the Cubs in free agency.
The 32-year-old Bregman got off to a rough start in his new home, hitting just .229 with two homers in his first 20 games. But he has been one of Chicago’s most productive players since the All-Star break, batting .305 with 17 homers and 48 RBIs in his last 57 games.
Bregman also has excelled in the postseason in the past. He won two World Series championships with the Houston Astros. He appeared in at least two postseason games in each of the previous nine years.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Dodgers have reinstated designated hitter/pitcher Shohei Ohtani from the injured list and left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list and optioned outfielder Josue De Paula and right-handed pitcher Kyle Hurt to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ohtani, 32, has been out since September 8 with right biceps discomfort. He has appeared in 134 games, slashing .277/.380/.522 with 30 homers and 80 RBI. He made 14 starts this season, posting an 8-2 record with a 1.79 ERA and 95 strikeouts. The back-to-back reigning National League MVP has been with the Dodgers three seasons, recording 19.1 bWAR with 139 homers, 312 RBI and a .990 OPS in 447 games at the plate and a 9-3 record with a 2.17 ERA on the mound. He has been in the Majors nine seasons, slashing .281/.375/.575 with 310 homers and 749 RBI while going 47-22 with a 2.83 ERA and 765 strikeouts in 114 games on the mound.
Skubal, 29, has made nine starts for the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers and he is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in 55 innings. On the season, he is 11-7 with a 2.85 ERA in 25 starts this season. The two-time Cy Young award winner has been in the Major Leagues seven seasons, posting a 65-44 record with a 3.04 ERA in 162 games (159 starts). He has 1,065 strikeouts in 918.1 innings while owning a 1.02 WHIP. He was drafted by the Tigers in the ninth round of the 2018 First Year Player Draft out of the University of Seattle.
De Paula, 21, appeared in 11 games for the Dodgers, batting .323 with one homer and seven RBI. Prior to joining the Dodgers, he was slashing .303/.401/.547 with 27 homers and 104 RBI in 124 games with Double-A Tulsa. He has played 462 minor league games across four levels, slashing .286/.404/.453 with 56 homers and 280 RBI. He signed with the Dodgers as an international free agent on January 15, 2022.
Hurt, 28, pitched two scoreless innings last night in the Dodgers 7-0 win. He is 4-1 with a 4.14 ERA this season and 58 strikeouts in 45.2 innings. He has been with the Dodgers three seasons, compiling a 3.64 ERA with 64 strikeouts in 54.1 innings and a 4-2 mark. The Southern California native was originally drafted by the Marlins in the fifth round of the 2020 First Year Player Draft out of the University of Southern California.
The Los Angeles Dodgers franchise, with nine World Series championships and 26 National League pennants since its beginnings in Brooklyn in 1890, is committed to a tradition of pride and excellence. The Dodgers, baseball’s 2024 and 2025 back-to-back World Champions, are the reigning Sports Business Journal Sports Team of the Year, have been recognized as ESPN’s Sports Humanitarian Team of the Year and are dedicated to supporting a culture of winning baseball, providing a first-class, fan-friendly experience, and building a strong partnership with the community. With the highest cumulative fan attendance in Major League Baseball history and a record of breaking barriers, the Dodgers are one of the most cherished sports franchises in the world. Visit the Dodgers online at www.dodgers.com, follow them on Twitter @Dodgers and like them on Facebook at www.facebook.com/Dodgers. For media information, visit www.dodgerspressbox.com.

item.content:encoded:
En medio de su peor año en las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB), el dominicano Vladimir Guerrero Jr. encendió la polémica al asegurar que los 500 millones de dólares que los Blue Jays le garantizaron en un contrato por 14 temporadas fue por lo que hizo, no por lo que podría hacer en el futuro.
¿Qué dijo Vladimir Guerrero Jr. sobre su contrato?
“El dinero que a mí me dieron, no fue por lo que voy a hacer, fue por lo que hice”, dijo Guerrero Jr. en una entrevista con Digital 15, refiriéndose al año pasado, cuando llevó al equipo a la Serie Mundial. “A mí no me pagaron porque yo voy a dar 40 (jonrones) todos los años, a mí me pagaron por lo que hice ya”.
Vladdy: hundido con los Blue Jays
Las declaraciones levantaron todo tipo de opiniones, especialmente porque Vladdy está en su temporada de números más bajos, excluyendo la recortada temporada del 2020. Su promedio de bateo (.263), jonrones (9) y carreras producidas (56) son sus peores cifras en cualquier año desde 2019, cuando debutó en las Grandes Ligas.
An emotional Vladimir Guerrero Jr. after a devastating World Series loss pic.twitter.com/xPUYsPORPX
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) November 2, 2025
La poca producción ofensiva repercutió directamente a los Blue Jays que, después de estar a centímetros de ganar la Serie Mundial, quedaron eliminados en la carrera por asegurar un lugar en los playoffs este 2026.
