item.content:encoded:
After three straight 100-loss seasons, the Chicago White Sox can clinch a spot in the American League playoffs tonight.
The White Sox (81-76) carry a magic number of two to earn a playoff berth as they try for a series victory against the host Kansas City Royals (67-90).
“Every night here on out, it’s playoff atmosphere baseball,” White Sox outfielder Randal Grichuk said.
Grichuk went 4-for-5 with a three-run home run and finished a triple shy of the cycle as Chicago outslugged Kansas City 14-11 in Tuesday’s series opener.
Chase Meidroth went deep as part of a 3-for-4, five-RBI showing, and Brenton Doyle and Munetaka Murakami also homered. The White Sox improved to 9-0 this season when they hit at least four home runs.
Chicago remained one game behind the A.L. Central-leading Cleveland Guardians while staying three games clear of the White Sox’s nearest competitor — the Texas Rangers — for the third and final A.L. wild-card spot. A White Sox win, plus a Rangers loss to the New York Mets today, would clinch at least a wild-card spot for Chicago.
White Sox starter Anthony Kay worked just four-plus innings Tuesday, but the offense picked up the slack with 13 hits.
Grichuk paced the attack. He is batting .373 with five doubles, a triple, three home runs and 11 RBI in September.
“I feel good. Mechanically, I feel good. Mentally, I’m in a good spot,” Grichuk said. “Hopefully, it can continue. This is when you want to be at your best, obviously. Playing meaningful games in September trying to get to October.”
Kansas City has lost five straight games and eight of nine but is coming off its best offensive output in nearly a month.
Tuesday marked the first time the Royals scored double-digit runs since a 13-2 victory at Toronto on Aug. 27.
Vinnie Pasquantino belted a ninth-inning grand slam to punctuate a 3-for-5, five-RBI night. Bobby Witt Jr. added three hits and Jac Caglianone had two.
Kansas City will turn tonight to right-hander Seth Lugo (7-9, 5.06 ERA), an 11-year veteran who is aiming to avoid his first career season with double-digit losses.
Lugo has worked five innings in each of his first three September starts. He took the 6-2 loss at Houston on Thursday, giving up four runs and eight hits with one walk and five strikeouts.
The Astros hit four solo home runs against Lugo, who has surrendered multiple long balls in a game six times this season.
“It sounds kind of strange, but I think his stuff was pretty crisp,” Royals manager Matt Quatraro said after that game. “He just missed on a couple, and they got him on first pitches.”
Lugo pitched effectively against the host White Sox on April 9 but lost 2-0 after allowing two runs (one earned) and four hits in 6 1/3 innings. He also was the losing pitcher in a 6-5 game in Chicago on May 13, giving up five runs on eight hits and two walks in five innings.
In eight career starts against the White Sox, including seven starts, Lugo is 3-2 with a 2.14 ERA over 46 1/3 innings.
Left-hander Bryan Hudson (5-4, 3.03 ERA) will serve as the opener tonight for Chicago ahead of right-hander Erick Fedde (8-9, 3.90), who has worked 10 innings over two starts against the Royals this season, going 0-1 with a 2.70 ERA. The loss came April 11, 2-0.
Fedde is 1-2 with a 2.84 ERA in five career starts vs. Kansas City covering 25 1/3 innings. He took a no-decision against the visiting Detroit Tigers last Thursday, permitting one run and four hits in 4 2/3 innings with two walks and six strikeouts in a 3-1 win.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Vladimir Guerrero Jr. tries to clarify answer about his $500 million contract after original response goes viral
item.dc:creator: Jack Baer
item.description: You won't find many people who disagree with the statement that Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is having a disappointing 2026 season. In fact, they may have words even more harsh for a first baseman with only one home run at his home ballpark this year. Through 141 games, Guerrero is slashing .263/.336/.359, with an OPS that ranks 23rd out of 26 qualified first basemen in MLB. He is doing this in the first season of a 14-year, $500 million contract that ranks as the third-largest in league history by gua
item.content:encoded:
You won't find many people who disagree with the statement that Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is having a disappointing 2026 season. In fact, they may have words even more harsh for a first baseman with only one home run at his home ballpark this year.
Through 141 games, Guerrero is slashing .263/.336/.359, with an OPS that ranks 23rd out of 26 qualified first basemen in MLB. He is doing this in the first season of a 14-year, $500 million contract that ranks as the third-largest in league history by guaranteed money.
Guerrero's underperformance looms large for a Blue Jays team that will miss the playoffs a year after reaching the World Series, especially looking forward given how much the franchise has invested in him. Which is why a recent comment made in a Spanish-language interview with Telemicro News didn't go down so well.
Guerrero's answer to a question about this season, translated by Héctor Gómez:
"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I'm going to do. I understand why the fans believe it's the other way around. Sometimes I think that way too, like 'Oh they give me this money and I'm not doing enough,' but you know I try my best and I'm working hard.
The fans I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you but when you are not at your best not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."
For those unfamiliar with the economics of sports teams, paying a player for past performance rather than what they will do — as Guerrero said the Blue Jays did — is the exact opposite of what front offices are supposed to do. If it worked the way Guerrero is suggesting, his teammate Max Scherzer would probably be guaranteed more than $3 million this season.
The statement went viral, with one thread on the Blue Jays subreddit getting more than 300 comments in less than three hours. They, largely, are not happy.
Guerrero, or the Blue Jays, apparently felt the heat enough that he spoke to reporters hours after the comment started circulating and attempted to give a better answer. His response, via Keegan Matheson of MLB.com:
"That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year. I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn't help my team get to the postseason. I said I felt — that it's my personal opinion — that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.
"To the fans, I've never stopped working very hard. I am going to go into the offseason again to prepare myself the best I can. Physically, mentally, everything that I have like I always do for my team and my teammates."
That's a bit better, but Guerrero actually doubles down on the idea that players are paid for past performance and tries to note that he signed his megadeal at the beginning of the 2025 season. It did not go into effect until this year, though, as Guerrero played out 2025 on his $28.5 million arbitration salary.
When asked, Guerrero said he didn't regret the comments and also hinted that he wasn't 100% healthy this year, but denied he had any major injuries.
The reality of the Blue Jays is that they bet on the 27-year-old Guerrero being a franchise-defining talent well into his 30s. It seemed like a reasonable goal when he slashed a monster .397/.494/.795 in last year's postseason, but now he and several of his teammates are underperforming relative to the incredible bar they set last October.
Guerrero tried to get around that awkwardness by suggesting an alternative way for contracts to be evaluated, but he's still got reality in front of him. The Blue Jays simply need him to get better, immediately.
The good news is that 2026 is only a single season, and he has bounced back from down years before. There are still things he does quite well, but he badly needs to rework an approach that has left him wanting for quality contact.

item.title: [MLB.com] Vlad Jr. expands on comments about his contract, disappointing season
item.dc:creator: Keegan Matheson
item.description: BALTIMORE -- It takes a lot for the Blue Jays’ 2026 elimination to dip below being the story of the day, but that’s exactly what happened Wednesday in Baltimore, as Vladimir Guerrero Jr. addressed some controversial quotes from a recent Spanish-language interview. In a conversation recently with Veronica Batista, Guerrero addressed his disappointing season and spoke about his 14-year, $500 million extension. Those comments didn’t sit well with fans, though, when Guerrero spoke about being paid f
item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE -- It takes a lot for the Blue Jays’ 2026 elimination to dip below being the story of the day, but that’s exactly what happened Wednesday in Baltimore, as Vladimir Guerrero Jr. addressed some controversial quotes from a recent Spanish-language interview.
In a conversation recently with Veronica Batista, Guerrero addressed his disappointing season and spoke about his 14-year, $500 million extension. Those comments didn’t sit well with fans, though, when Guerrero spoke about being paid for what he’s done for the Blue Jays in the past, not what he’s expected to do in the future.
“I want people to understand one thing,” Guerrero said in Spanish. “The money they gave me wasn’t for what I’m going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn’t pay me because I’m going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself: bro, they gave you all that money and you’re out here doing nothing. I try.”
Asked about those comments following the Blue Jays being mathematically eliminated from the playoffs Wednesday afternoon, Guerrero stood by them.
"No, I don't regret myself. I'm not lying with what I say,” Guerrero said through interpreter Hector Lebron. “I understand some fans, they don't understand the way and what I was trying to say specifically, but what I said is the way I feel."
This takes us back to the lessons learned in Spring Training of 2025, when Guerrero and the Blue Jays were first negotiating his $500 million extension.
Every few days, another Spanish-language podcast or television appearance featuring Guerrero would be released, often with journalists or interviewers from his native Dominican Republic. It’s important to ensure that nothing is lost in translation, first and foremost, then to contextualize when and why these things were said.
Last spring, for example, a couple of those interviews lingered for weeks at a time before being posted, which stirred up more discourse than anyone -- perhaps even Guerrero -- had planned.
This time, Guerrero’s comments days later seemed to line up with his initial interview with Batista, which was making its rounds on social media throughout Wednesday’s Game 1 of the doubleheader. At one point, Guerrero was also asked to expand on those comments and explain why he was thinking that.
“That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year. I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason,” Guerrero said. “I said I felt -- that it’s my personal opinion -- that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.”
Getting Guerrero right is the Blue Jays’ No. 1 priority this offseason. It might be No. 2 and No. 3, as well. If he’s hitting 40-plus home runs, then the Blue Jays might have more of an appetite for moments like this, but it lands at a particularly rough time, given the season he’s just had. Guerrero has hit just nine home runs this season with an OPS that’s been hovering below .700.
“He’s got all the potential in the world. We know that. We’ve seen him be one of, if not the best, players in the game,” John Schneider said. “Years like this, they can happen. Myself, the staff and Vlad, he’s not chalking this one up to ‘one of those years.’ He worked tirelessly to get out of the funk he was in. He tried new things. He tried different ways to prepare and he posted every single day. Definitely not what we expected, what he expected. It’s not what we expect out of him going forward and not what he expects out of himself going forward.”

item.title: [Away Back Gone] Crazy Steven Kwan stat makes his rough start to Guardians' season seem like ages ago
item.dc:creator: Henry Palattella
item.description: On May 23, Steven Kwan went 0-for-3 against the Philadelphia Phillies. In years prior, that kind of outcome would have been an anomaly for Kwan, who routinely ranked among baseball’s best at getting on base. That wasn’t the case at the start of this season, however, as that hitless outing against the Phillies dropped Kwan’s batting average to .196. item.content:encoded:
On May 23, Steven Kwan went 0-for-3 against the Philadelphia Phillies. In years prior, that kind of outcome would have been an anomaly for Kwan, who routinely ranked among baseball’s best at getting on base.
That wasn’t the case at the start of this season, however, as that hitless outing against the Phillies dropped Kwan’s batting average to .196. Not only did it look like Kwan was playing his way out of the Guardians’ future, but it also seemed like there was a chance they could consider the nuclear option and cut him loose during the season.
But then a funny thing happened. He got some hits. A three-hit game the next day in the series finale. A two-hit game against the Yankees on the first day of June. Seven hits in three games against the Pirates in the middle of June.
Pretty soon the Guardians were winning, and Kwan was back to being a force at the top of the lineup.
When Kwan walked back to the dugout after grounding out in his final at-bat on May 23, it looked like it was going to be a lost season for both him and the Guardians.
When Kwan digs into the batter’s box later today against the Red Sox, he’ll do so with the 11th-best on-base percentage in MLB (.378) for a Guardians team that has a Magic Number of 2.
If Kwan is able to keep things up, it’s out of the realm of possibility that he could finish the season in the top 10 in on-base percentage. Not bad for a guy who spent the first two months of the season as one of the worst qualified hitters in baseball.
The Guardians are a much more dangerous team now that Steven Kwan is back to being productive
It’s not an understatement to say that Kwan’s return to form has helped push the Guardians back into the postseason picture. He was an easy out early in the season, and it got so bad the Guardians moved him out of the leadoff spot for the first time since he was thrust into the spot after he made his debut in 2022.
The craziest part of the whole process is that Kwan didn’t change a ton about his process — he just wasn’t doing the things that helped turn him into an on-base machine.
It seems like his change was much mental as it was physical (though it also seemed like he shifted his focus to peppering the ball all over the outfield as opposed to trying to pull the ball).
Regardless of what it was, it seems clear that Kwan is back. His .324 batting average in the 97 games since that hitless performance against the Phillies is tied for the best mark in MLB while his .410 on-base percentage is third.
Williams has been a mainstay atop the Guardians’ lineup in all three of their postseason appearances since he made his big league debut.
Although we don’t know when the Guardians are going to make their postseason debut this season, we know that Kwan is going to be atop their lineup when they do. And they’re going to be better for it.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have already clinched the NL Central, but with five regular-season games remaining, they’re still trying to capture the No. 1 overall seed. They currently hold the top spot in the National League.
After losing to the Philadelphia Phillies on Tuesday night, they hold just a one-game lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers for the top seed in the NL.
On Wednesday night, they’ll play the second game of their series against the Phillies, with right-handed pitcher Aaron Nola on the mound against Brewers righty Logan Henderson.
Brewers Make Christian Yelich Move
Ahead of the matchup, Brewers manager Pat Murphy made a few changes to his starting lineup, one of which involves veteran Christian Yelich.
After batting sixth in the order on Tuesday, Yelich will drop one spot and hit seventh, batting in front of Sal Frelick and David Hamilton. He’ll once again serve as the team’s designated hitter.
Here’s the full Brewers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Brewers 9/23 G. Mitchell CF J. Chourio LF B. Turang 2B W. Contreras C J. Bauers 1B J. Ortiz SS C. Yelich DH S. Frelick RF D. Hamilton 3B L. Henderson SP.”
Brewers 9/23
G. Mitchell CF
J. Chourio LF
B. Turang 2B
W. Contreras C
J. Bauers 1B
J. Ortiz SS
C. Yelich DH
S. Frelick RF
D. Hamilton 3B
L. Henderson SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 23, 2026
Looking at Yelich’s 2026 Season
In his 14th MLB season, Yelich has taken a step back in terms of being the everyday player he once was.
Across 114 games in 2026, Yelich is hitting .235 in 430 at-bats. He’s recorded 67 runs, 101 hits, 11 home runs, and 57 RBIs while slugging .374 with a .688 OPS.
Brewers Right Now
Milwaukee is 98-59 overall with the best record in baseball. And will play two more games against the Phillies before wrapping up the regular season with a three-game set against the St. Louis Cardinals beginning Friday.
The Brewers have already clinched at least a first-round bye. However, earning the No. 1 seed would give them home-field advantage throughout the postseason.

item.title: [heraldglobe.com] Orioles win Game 1, eliminate Blue Jays from wild-card chase
item.description:

The Blue Jays (77-81) were the reigning American League champions, but they won't have a chance to return to the World Series. The Orioles (77-81) must win the nightcap of the day-night twinbill
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

24 Sep 2026, 02:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jamie LeBlanc)
Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit another home run and the Orioles eliminated the visiting Toronto Blue Jays from playoff contention by winning 4-2 on Wednesday afternoon in the first game of a doubleheader.
The Blue Jays (77-81) were the reigning American League champions, but they won't have a chance to return to the World Series.
The Orioles (77-81) must win the nightcap of the day-night twinbill in order to stay alive for an AL wild-card spot, though if the Chicago White Sox win in Kansas City later Wednesday, that would bump Baltimore from contention.
Chris Bassitt (9-5) pitched five-plus innings to notch a victory in his third consecutive start. He was charged with two runs on seven hits with one walk.
Andrew Kittredge, the fourth reliever for the Orioles, worked the ninth for his 11th save.
Max Scherzer (3-9) took the loss as he was charged with four runs and four hits in five innings.
Ernie Clement and Andres Gimenez both had two hits, including a double each, for the Blue Jays. Toronto finished with 10 hits, leaving eight runners on base.
The doubleheader was necessary after Tuesday night's scheduled game was postponed.
Jeremiah Jackson's single gave Baltimore the game's first run in the second. Colton Cowser later scored when Jackson was caught attempting to steal second base.
Alonso's two-run blast pushed the margin to 4-0 in the fifth inning. His 41st homer of the season was his third of the series, which began with his two-homer outing Monday night when the Orioles rallied for a 4-3 victory.
Toronto scored two runs on the same play in the sixth inning, both charged to Bassitt. Brandon Valenzuela's two-out infield single pushed in a run and second baseman Jackson's throwing error allowed a second run to score.
Alonso's homer was one of five Baltimore hits. The others were singles. The Orioles won Monday's game with six hits.
Three Toronto relievers limited Baltimore to no runs with one hit.
--Field Level Media

There's good news to report on both fronts, as manager Walt Weiss is planning on Robert Suarez making his first big league appearance following his activation from a long stint on the IL and that Ronald Acuña Jr. is reportedly feeling fine after suffering a left shin contusion on Tuesday night. Acuña is out of the lineup tonight bu
item.content:encoded:
The lineups are out for tonight's middle game between the Atlanta Braves and the Cincinnati Reds and the big news as far as Atlanta concerned was focused on injuries. There's good news to report on both fronts, as manager Walt Weiss is planning on Robert Suarez making his first big league appearance following his activation from a long stint on the IL and that Ronald Acuña Jr. is reportedly feeling fine after suffering a left shin contusion on Tuesday night. Acuña is out of the lineup tonight but he's no longer walking with a limp, so obviously some rest and (presumably) some ice did him well overnight.
In fact, it was to the point that Weiss reportedly stated during the pregame press conference that Acuña was apparently trying to convince the skipper to put him in the lineup for tonight's game. Obviously with an eye on the Postseason, that was never going to happen but it's nonetheless a good sign about how Acuña is feeling at the moment. Mark Bowman of MLB.com shared the report on social media.
Needless to say, the Atlanta Braves are going to need both Acuña and Suarez healthy and ready to go for October if they're going to have the best chance possible at making a deep Postseason run. Ever since Acuña reportedly widened his stance back on August 26, he's been hitting at a .348/.408/.641 clip with a .445 wOBA and 184 wRC+. Meanwhile, Suarez was carrying a 0.56 ERA and a 2.44 FIP across 32 innings pitched before he went on the IL following his appearance on June 19.
If both of those guys can keep up that pace upon their respective returns from injury then the Braves are going to be in a good spot heading into the Postseason. We'll see what happens going forward!

item.title: [MLB.com] Alonso crushes 41st homer, 1st off Scherzer as Orioles stave off elimination vs. Blue Jays
item.dc:creator: Jake Rill
item.description: BALTIMORE -- After being named the unanimous winner of the 2026 Most Valuable Oriole Award on Wednesday morning, Pete Alonso took the field at Camden Yards and continued what is shaping up to be an incredible finish to his first year in Baltimore. Alonso belted his 41st home run of the season to lift the Orioles to a 4-2 victory over the Blue Jays in Game 1 of a split doubleheader. It marked the Polar Bear’s third homer over the first two games of this American League East rivalry series, as he
item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE -- After being named the unanimous winner of the 2026 Most Valuable Oriole Award on Wednesday morning, Pete Alonso took the field at Camden Yards and continued what is shaping up to be an incredible finish to his first year in Baltimore.
Alonso belted his 41st home run of the season to lift the Orioles to a 4-2 victory over the Blue Jays in Game 1 of a split doubleheader. It marked the Polar Bear’s third homer over the first two games of this American League East rivalry series, as he swatted a pair in Monday night’s 4-3 comeback win.
It also helped the O’s stay alive in the AL Wild Card race for at least a bit longer. With an elimination number of one, Baltimore would be eliminated with either a loss in Game 2 of the twin bill against Toronto or via a White Sox win at Kansas City.
Although the Orioles may not end up in the playoffs, they continue to feel great about what Alonso has brought to the club -- and what the 31-year-old slugger should bring throughout the remainder of the five-year, $155 million contract he signed this past December.
Alonso is one of only eight players to hit 41 or more homers in a season in O’s history (since 1954), posting the ninth such campaign overall. His AL-high 110 RBIs are the most by a Baltimore player since Chris Davis had 117 in 2015.
The only AL players with as many homers as Alonso this season are Houston’s Yordan Alvarez and Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero, who each entered Wednesday with 41.
With nine home runs over his past 18 games (and 18 homers in 41 games since Aug. 9), Alonso is continuing to climb the Orioles’ all-time single-season home run leaderboard. Next on the list is Rafael Palmeiro, who hit 43 in 1998.
Alonso, who has started every game this season, has four more games to add to his homer total -- Wednesday’s nightcap vs. the Blue Jays, followed by a three-game set against the Yankees in New York this weekend.
Despite the large contract and even larger expectations, Alonso said he hasn’t felt any added pressure to perform in 2026.
“It’s not trying to be anything different or anything more or less than who I am and what I can bring on a day-to-day basis,” Alonso said. “There’s a lot of comfort and peace of mind in that, where it’s like, ‘Hey, we believe in you, not just from a player’s side, but what you bring as a personality and teammate.’ For me, that speaks volumes.
“For me, it’s just justification. It’s like, ‘Hey, who you are, we need that, and we appreciate what you do.’ And they’re just like, ‘Go be yourself.’ What that entails is just being the best you can on the field between the lines and the best teammate you can be every single day. I really appreciate the runway, obviously.”
All season, Alonso’s leadership has drawn as much praise as his on-field performance.
“The biggest thing that stands out with Pete is, yeah, he’s going out there and competing, he wants to go out there and produce for the team, but he also wants everyone around him to do the same thing,” manager Craig Albernaz said. “He wants to help. He wants to pull everyone in the right direction, for the team and to win games.”
Alonso’s two-run blast in the fifth inning in Wednesday’s opener was his first off veteran right-hander Max Scherzer, his Mets teammate during the 2022 and ‘23 seasons. Alonso was previously 4-for-25 (.160) with two doubles, one walk and 12 strikeouts lifetime vs. Scherzer.
Right-hander Chris Bassitt turned in another solid outing, allowing two earned runs over five-plus innings. Although the 37-year-old had a 4.59 ERA in 20 games (18 starts), he recorded a 3.74 ERA over his final eight outings after returning from a back injury in mid-August.
Bassitt, who was also teammates with Alonso in New York in 2022, hasn’t been surprised at all by Alonso’s performance this season.
“Pete deserves MVP votes, and he deserves them every single year. That’s just the reality. He’s one of the most underappreciated players in our game. He’s easily a top three hitter every single year,” Bassitt said. “He’s not having a crazy historical year for his standards. It’s just Pete being Pete, and people are like, ‘Dang, this is really, really special.’ But he’s been doing that for years.
“Pete just held the standard of what he’s done for years, and I think people are now realizing, ‘Holy [crap], this guy’s really good.’ But he’s always been really, really good. So yeah, it’s Pete being Pete.”

item.content:encoded:
At this point, it seems that Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is going to run away with the National League MVP award.
On Wednesday, MLB insider Jon Heyman even had a bold prediction regarding Crow-Armstrong’s MVP case, saying he should be the unanimous winner.
“He’s having an all-time great season,” Heyman said. “He has just been incredible…He is the unanimous NL MVP, there’s no question about that.”
Shohei Ohtani, who was considered the other NL MVP favorite, has been dealing with injuries. He was the only player to ever win a unanimous MVP more than once.
PCA is the unanimous NL MVP, according to @JonHeyman 🏆⭐️ pic.twitter.com/MKQdPylA1f
— B/R Walk-Off (@BRWalkoff) September 23, 2026
It’s a rare feat to be the unanimous MVP winner, and it has happened only 24 times, according to MLB.com.
Going into Wednesday’s game, Crow-Armstrong has a .282 average with 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs scored and 39 stolen bases, so he is one stolen base away from a 40-40 season.
As Heyman mentioned, Crow-Armstrong could also be the first player to lead his league in offensive and defensive WAR.
The Cubs are still fighting to secure a Wild Card spot, and they entered Wednesday in a three-way tie with the San Diego padres and Philadelphia Phillies for the top spot of the Wild Card race.
Yet, barring a massive surprise, it seems that Pete Crow-Armstrong has the NL MVP award locked up.

item.content:encoded:
Framber Valdez lost to the Nationals after allowing two runs in 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday.

Valdez opened with five scoreless innings today to lower his ERA from 4.06 to 3.94, but he gave up three straight singles to start the sixth, with his one out coming because of a baserunning miscue. He was lifted down 1-0, with his ERA sitting at 3.98. However, the remaining runner came around to score off Tyler Kinley, pushing Valdez’s ERA back up to 4.03 to end the year. He also fell to 10-12. The collapse of his strikeout rate this year seems like a bad sign going forward, but at least he did turn back into a very strong groundball pitcher over the last four months. He might be through as a top-20 fantasy starter, but he should still offer some mixed-league value next year.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Pirates Make Surprising Oneil Cruz Decision Before Cardinals Game

item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Pirates have benefited greatly from center fielder Oneil Cruz in their lineup, which makes this latest lineup decision perplexing.
Cruz won't start for the Pirates in their next game against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on Sept. 23, as Jake Mangum takes his place in center field.
It marks the first time Cruz hasn't started a game since Aug. 23 in a 4-0 loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium.
The Pirates won't have Cruz in their lineup for a month and 25 games, so they'll need others to step up.
Why it's Odd Cruz Isn't Starting vs. Cardinals
Pittsburgh faces St. Louis left-handed pitcher Matthew Liberatore in this one, and it's no secret the struggles they've had against southpaws this season.
The Pirates have an 18-32 record against left-handed starting pitching, compared to 62-45 against right-handed pitching.
Cruz has been the Pirates' best hitter against southpaws, batting .323/.373/.476 for an OPS of .849, with 40 hits in 124 at-bats, five doubles, a triple, four home runs and 19 RBI.
He took time this offseason to fix his approach against lefties, working with a left-handed pitcher in batting practice, and it's been a massive improvement, after he hit .102 last season.
Cruz has also been successful against Liberatore this season, with three hits in six at-bats, including a double and an RBI.
The Pirates have hit well against Libertatore in 2026, scoring four runs over 4.2 innings on May 19 and three runs over 5.2 innings on Aug. 30, both at Busch Stadium.
Cruz is more than a month removed from his official return from his left-hand fracture, so he's still dealing with pain.
He's been great since returning, hitting .309/.402/.518 for an OPS of .920 in 30 games, with 34 hits in 110 at-bats, three doubles, a triple, six home runs, 23 RBI and seven stolen bases.
The Pirates are also eliminated from postseason contention, so they can give him a rest day instead of pushing him.
Pirates Lineup vs. Cardinals and Liberatore
| Player | Position | Batting Side |
|---|---|---|
| Konnor Griffin | Shortstop | Right |
| Rafael Flores Jr. | Catcher | Right |
| Bryan Reynolds | Left Fielder | Switch |
| Brandon Lowe | Second Base | Left |
| Nick Gonzales | Designated Hitter | Right |
| Ronny Simon | Right Fielder | Switch |
| Ryan O'Hearn | First Base | Left |
| Jared Triolo | Third Base | Right |
| Jake Mangum | Center Fielder | Switch |
The Pirates have just two left-handed hitters vs. Liberatore, second baseman Brandon Lowe and first baseman Ryan O'Hearn.
Lowe will bat fourth for just the third time this season, last doing so vs. the Dodgers on Aug. 23 and also in an 8-3 win over the Boston Red Sox at PNC Park on Aug. 13.
O'Hearn bats seventh for just the second time this season, first doing it in a 6-5 win over the Kansas City Royals at PNC Park on Sept. 19.
Catcher Rafael Flores Jr. bats second for the first time in his career, the highest he's ever been in an MLB lineup.
Shortstop Konnor Griffin bats leadoff, third baseman Jared Triolo bats seventh and designated hitter Nick Gonzales bats fifth.
Left fielder Bryan Gonzales stays third, right fielder Ronny Simon hits sixth and Mangum bats ninth against the Cardinals.
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

They're coming off a 3-2 loss against the Minnesota Twins on Tuesday night and sit at 65-93 overall with just five games remaining in the regular season. And while these games don't count for anything and it's likely most in San Francisco are eagerly awaiting the end of the season, the Giants still have a lot of young talent on the big league team to check out over these final few days, which brings some
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco Giants certainly have not had the season they'd hoped for by any stretch.
They're coming off a 3-2 loss against the Minnesota Twins on Tuesday night and sit at 65-93 overall with just five games remaining in the regular season.
And while these games don't count for anything and it's likely most in San Francisco are eagerly awaiting the end of the season, the Giants still have a lot of young talent on the big league team to check out over these final few days, which brings some intrigue.
Giants Make Marcelo Mayer Move
At the top of that list is infielder Marcelo Mayer, whom the Giants acquired in an Aug. 4 trade with the Boston Red Sox.
Mayer, a former top prospect for the Red Sox, is currently 23 years old and was injured before the trade, so he was finally activated on Monday and made his Giants debut.
In his four at-bats on Monday, though, he struck out all four times, which led to a day off Tuesday as he was out of the lineup.
Despite that, Giants manager Tony Vitello has inserted Mayer back into the starting nine on Wednesday afternoon, and he'll bat seventh in the order while serving as the designated hitter.
Here's the full Giants lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Updated Giants 9/23 J. Cox 2B T. Hill CF V. Bericoto LF B. Davidson RF A. Knizner C B. Harris 1B M. Mayer DH S. Whitcomb 3B C. Koss SS C. Perdomo SP."
Mayer's MLB Career
After emerging as a highly sought-after prospect and working his way up to the Red Sox major league team fairly quickly, Mayer never really found much success during his two seasons in Boston.
He appeared in 114 games with the Red Sox and hit .223, recording 39 runs, 74 hits, seven home runs, and 32 RBIs in 332 at-bats.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.content:encoded:
The Texas Rangers are fighting for their playoff lives as they enter into the second game of a three-game series with the New York Mets.
Texas dropped the first game of the series, hurting their chances of getting into the playoffs. But this second game does offer them another chance to salvage the season and get into the dance.
The Rangers are looking to defend home field in the final series at Globe Life Field during the regular season. But the Mets are a feisty team who will be trying to play spoiler for Texas in this matchup.
Rangers Announce Corey Seager Move
Ahead of the game against the Mets, the Rangers have released the lineup. Within the lineup, slugger Corey Seager will be batting second for Texas.
Seager will be taking on the shortstop role in this game.
Rangers 9/23
W. Langford LF
C. Seager SS
J. Jung DH
B. Nimmo RF
E. Duran 3B
J. Burger 1B
N. Lopez 2B
D. Jansen C
E. Carter CF
C. Bradford SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 23, 2026
Seager has hit .229 with 18 home runs and 47 RBIs this season, with an OPS of .739. 2026 has been a down year for the slugger, but he did miss a lot of time due to injury.
If the Rangers are going to get into the playoffs, Seager will need to be a big reason why. So, if he can put together a solid run over these final few games, Texas may have a good chance to get into the postseason.
Can Rangers Get Into Playoffs?
After falling short in the first game to the Mets, the Rangers’ chances have dropped a little. But the team isn’t giving up, and they will look to bounce back in the second game.
“I don’t think we played nervous,” manager Skip Schumaker said. “As far as nerves, no, I don’t think they were nervous. It was just a couple of misplays. … I think you’re used to seeing those plays made. They’re really good. They play fundamentally sound. They’ve been playing fundamentally sound baseball. We made a couple miscues tonight that cost us, and that’s part of the reason why we lost. So again, that’s why we have to flush it.”
The Rangers are looking to get into the playoffs as either the AL West champions or as a wild-card team. But at this point, the AL West may be the best bet for this group.
Texas is currently tied with the Houston Astros for the division lead, with Houston holding the tiebreaker. So, over the final few games, the Rangers are going to need to bring their best performance if they want to get into the playoffs.
Taking care of business against the Mets will be crucial if this team wants to reach the postseason. And then, after the series with New York, Texas will be heading on the road for a massive series against the Minnesota Twins.
It’s put up or shut up time for the Rangers, and if they can’t get it together, they could be on the outside looking in once again.

item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday night, the Atlanta Braves will continue their series against the Cincinnati Reds at Truist Park.
Most recently, the Braves lost 4-0 in the series opener on Tuesday.
Austin Riley went 1-for-4 while batting seventh in the loss.
Atlanta Braves Announce Austin Riley Change
Ahead of the second game of the series, the Atlanta Braves announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB posted on X: “Braves 9/23 D. Baldwin C M. Dubón LF M. Olson 1B O. Albies 2B M. Harris II CF A. Riley 3B S. Murphy DH B. Hicklen RF H. Kim SS C. Sale SP”
For only the second time in the last 52 games, Austin Riley will feature in the top six of the lineup. He has mostly batted out of the seven or eight spot in the lineup during this stretch.
Perhaps he was moved up with the absence of Ronald Acuña Jr. who departed Tuesday’s game after fouling a ball off himself.
It has been a tough season for the All-Star third baseman. He had previously been a top of the order caliber bat for the Braves, but his struggles have seen him moved down this season.
Overall, he’s batting a career-low .220 with 121 hits, 21 doubles, two triples, 17 home runs, 62 runs, 69 RBIs and nine stolen bases in 154 games.
Braves Right Now
At 92-65, the Atlanta Braves have already clinched the National League East. However, they remain behind the Milwaukee Brewers and Los Angeles Dodgers, which means the Braves will likely not have a first-round bye in the postseason. The Braves have gone 6-4 over their last 10 games.
Left-hander Chris Sale is set to make what is likely his final regular season start. He enters Wednesday’s game with a 14-9 record and a 2.18 ERA in 157.1 innings.
Reds Right Now
Meanwhile, the Cincinnati Reds have also announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB posted on X: “Reds 9/23 J. Brito RF E. De La Cruz SS S. Stewart 1B D. Myers CF E. Suárez DH M. McLain 2B O. Cabrera LF W. Banfield C K. Hayes 3B A. Abbott SP”
At 73-84, the Reds have already been eliminated from playoff contention. They have gone 4-6 over their last 10 games.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox kept outfielder Jarren Duran out of the starting lineup again Wednesday night as they hosted the Cleveland Guardians in the second game of a three-game series at Fenway Park.
Manager Chad Tracy’s posted batting order featured Roman Anthony in left field, Nick Sogard at first base, Jahmai Jones as the designated hitter, Wilyer Abreu in right field, Adley Rutschman behind the plate, Ceddanne Rafaela in center field, Caleb Durbin at third base, Trevor Story at shortstop and Andruw Monasterio at second base. Sonny Gray was listed as the starting pitcher.
Duran also sat Tuesday, when the Guardians beat the Red Sox 3-2. He entered that game as a pinch-hitter and drew a walk.
Cleveland took the series opener on Nathaniel Lowe’s sacrifice fly in the ninth inning. The Guardians stranded 15 runners but still extended their winning streak to six games.
Boston dropped to 84-73. The club already clinched an American League Wild Card berth Sunday but has lost three straight and eight of its last 12.
Duran entered Wednesday batting .204 with 110 hits, 20 home runs, 69 RBIs, 65 runs and 19 stolen bases in 146 games. He had 538 at-bats, 39 walks and 163 strikeouts.
The left-handed hitter has struggled in September. He was 9-for-50 with one home run and one RBI in 17 games this month before Tuesday’s appearance.
Over his last 15 games he was 8-for-42 with one homer. His on-base-plus-slugging percentage sat at .625 for the season.
Rafaela’s return to center field tightened the outfield picture. Anthony has been starting in left and Abreu in right, leaving Duran as the extra outfielder in many recent games.
Tracy had the interim tag removed Tuesday and was named the franchise’s 49th manager. The Red Sox have used a mix of platoons and rest days for Duran down the stretch.
Gray brings a 17-5 record and 2.82 ERA into the start. Cleveland is expected to counter with Forrest Griffin.
The Guardians sit at 82-75 and hold a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox in the AL Central. Chicago owns the season-series tiebreaker.
Duran, 30, is in his sixth major league season, all with Boston. He was an All-Star in 2024.
He still ranks among the team leaders in home runs and RBIs despite the low batting average. His 20 homers leave him one short of his career high.
The Red Sox close the regular season with this series, then host the Chicago Cubs for three games. Seeding and rest for the Wild Card round remain in play.
Duran’s speed and defense have kept him in the mix even as his batting average dropped. He stole 19 bases and continued to play a plus outfield when used.
Boston’s offense produced eight hits Tuesday. Rutschman went 3-for-4 and pinch-hitter Mickey Gasper tied the game with a home run in the eighth.
Cleveland collected 12 hits. Angel Martínez finished 3-for-4.
The Red Sox sit 12 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East. The Yankees hold the other Wild Card spot six games ahead of Boston.
Duran’s role for the final week and any postseason series will depend on how Tracy balances the four outfielders available.

However, he had one walk off the bench.

Duran remains out of the lineup on Wednesday.
He is currently batting .204 with 110 hits, 20 home runs, 69 RBIs, 65 runs and 19 stolen bases in 146 games this year.
The former All-Star is in the middle of his 6th MLB season (all with the Red Sox).
Looking At The Red Sox Right Now
The Red Sox are the third-place team in the American League East with an 84-73 record in 157 games.
They have lost six out of their last ten games (and are 38-38 in 76 games at home).
Talkin’ Yanks wrote (on Tuesday): “Yankees have clinched a higher seed than the Red Sox, which means they will host Boston in the three-game Wild Card series in the likely event that the two teams meet in the postseason next Tuesday through Thursday”
Following two more games with the Guardians, the Red Sox will finish the regular season against the Chicago Cubs (at home).
ESPN’s Buster Olney wrote: “The current thinking among the powers that be is that the Cubs and Red Sox will play a doubleheader Friday, and then an afternoon game Saturday.”
Looking At The Guardians
The Guardians are the top team in the American League Central with an 82-75 record in 157 games.
They are just 1.0 game ahead of the Chicago White Sox (who are in second).
Following the Red Sox, the Guardians will finish the 2026 regular season when they visit the Kansas City Royals.

Corbin Carroll and his Arizona Diamondbacks will take on the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field, on Wednesday, Sept. 23 at 8:40 p.m. ET. Carroll has +390 odds to hit a home run as of Wednesday afternoon.
What It Means
Carroll is hitting for a .240 BA, .331 OBP and .471 SLG with a 22.6% strikeout rate and an 11.1% walk rate. His OPS is .801 and he has scored 90 runs. In 650 plate appearances, he has hit 22 home runs and driven in 73 runs. Carroll has recorded 21 steals on 24 attempts. He had a one-hit showing in his last game (1-for-4) against the Rockies.
Mason Adams makes the start for the Rockies, his sixth of the season. He is 0-1 with a 5.09 ERA and 23 strikeouts in 23 2/3 innings pitched.

item.content:encoded:
Orioles get fortunate Jackson Holliday injury update amid Blue Jays series originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Baltimore Orioles second baseman Jackson Holliday landed on the injured list last week with left wrist inflammation.
Holliday's season is likely over, as the Orioles have just four games left to play after this afternoon's contest against the Toronto Blue Jays.
One more loss would eliminate Baltimore from postseason contention.
According to MLB.com's Jake Rill, Holliday's injury is more serious that orignally thought.
"Orioles' Jackson Holliday said he's going to need surgery on his left wrist. Either later this week or next week," Rill wrote on X. "Been told to expect about a 10-week recovery. Shouldn't impact 2027 timeline."
Rill's report indicates that Holliday should be ready for spring training in February. Obviously, this is a positive update for the Orioles.
However, the former top prospect has yet to live up to expectations, posting a .640 OPS in 354 plate appearances this season.
Holliday cannot be blamed entirely for Baltimore's struggles this season, but he does play a factor in its inability to create momentum towards a postseason berth.
He didn't make his season debut until May due to hamate bone surgery in the spring.
After a 17-homer and 17 stolen-base season in 2025, the 22-year-old managed just seven homers and eight stolen bases with an 83 OPS+ in 98 games.
Next season, the Orioles are hoping Holliday takes a big offensive leap following his recovery from wrist surgery.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Ronald Acuña Jr. Is Back in MVP Form
item.dc:creator: Tom Verducci
item.description: This article is a part of Verducci’s View, a new weekly baseball newsletter from Sports Illustrated senior writer Tom Verducci. item.content:encoded:
This article is a part of Verducci’s View, a new weekly baseball newsletter from Sports Illustrated senior writer Tom Verducci. Every Monday, Tom empties out his notebook over email and covers MLB’s hottest topics, provides in-depth analysis through both text and video breakdowns, looks forward to what’s worth watching during the week and more.
Ronald Acuña Jr. of the Braves may be hitting .259 with career lows in exit velocity and hard-hit rate, but don’t be fooled by the overall stats. If the star outfielder can fight through a left shin contusion he suffered Tuesday night on a foul ball at the plate—he’s currently considered day-to-day—he’ll be a force to be reckoned with in October. Ever since mid-August when Acuña began to knock off the rust from two IL stints, he’s been a dangerous, dynamic hitter.
The tell-tale sign is how Acuña is getting to high fastballs he used to miss.
| Acuna vs. 95+ MPH | No. | BA | SLG | HR | Attack Angle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Through Aug. 22 | 315 | .183 | .268 | 1 | 9° |
| Since | 119 | .393 | .857 | 4 | 7° |
Pitchers were dominating Acuña with velocity over his hands. No more. Acuña has made the adjustment. While his barrel had been working underneath the pitch plane, now he is flattening his attack angle, as you can see here:
Acuña heads my list of hitters who are most likely to cap a disappointing year with a strong finish.
Down Year but Primed for Big October
1. Ronald Acuña Jr., Braves
2. Mookie Betts, Dodgers
3. Will Smith, Dodgers
4. Trevor Story, Red Sox
5. José Ramírez, Guardians
Gerrit Cole, Game 2 Starter?
Yankees righthander Gerrit Cole broke through a late-season slump with an improved outing Friday in Arizona (six innings, two earned runs).
As I said last week here, Cole has been throwing too many strikes in the middle of the plate. His fix: tighten the delivery to be more compact and move almost six inches on the rubber toward the third base side.
A frequent tinkerer, Cole began the season toward the center of the rubber but after the Red Sox pounded him for four runs June 27, he moved to the first base side July 3 and stayed there for 13 starts. But after his poor start Sept. 12 against the Mets, which included a career high of hard hits, he returned to the center.
Here you can see his foot position change on the rubber in his past two starts:
It’s the quickest fix to a command issue. You don’t need to change mechanics, just the lane in which the ball leaves your hand.
How did it work? His command was much better. Look at his fastball heat maps and it’s clear he did a better job of keeping the ball out of the center lane:
Cole Fastball Heat Maps
This start moved Cole closer to getting the ball ahead of Max Fried or Carlos Rodon (or both) in a wild-card series against Boston.
As usual, Cole pounded the zone. He has not issued a walk among 71 batters faced in his past three starts. But still a concern: the swing-and-miss still has not returned to his game. He had only six swings-and-misses against Arizona. His September whiff rate is 17%, down from 22.4% entering the month.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone will have a difficult decision in choosing who starts after Schlittler, a decision that should be based on how Cole, Fried and Rodon are throwing the ball rather than sheer numbers or opponent trends. The Red Sox are slightly better against left-handed pitching (24–15, .746 OPS) than right-handed (60–55, .713 OPS), though the return of Roman Anthony changes that a bit.
📺 TV on TV This Week
Sunday, Sept. 27: Postseason Preview, 8 p.m. ET (MLB Network)
Up to 53 pressure-packed games in 33 days. The best month in all of sports is just about here.
I’ll’ll also be recording a playoff preview show on Monday along with MLB editor Will Laws and staff writer Ryan Phillips. Look out for that on our
Tom Verducci is a senior writer for Sports Illustrated who has covered Major League Baseball since 1981. He also serves as an analyst for FOX Sports and the MLB Network; is a New York Times best-selling author; and cohosts The Book of Joe podcast with Joe Maddon. A five-time Emmy Award winner across three categories (studio analyst, reporter, short form writing) and nominated in a fourth (game analyst), he is a three-time National Sportswriter of the Year winner, two-time National Magazine Award finalist, and a Penn State Distinguished Alumnus Award recipient. Verducci is a member of the National Sports Media Hall of Fame, Baseball Writers Association of America (including past New York chapter chairman) and a Baseball Hall of Fame voter since 1993. He also is the only writer to be a game analyst for World Series telecasts. He lives in New Jersey with his wife, with whom he has two children.

item.content:encoded:
Yordan Alvarez, Jacob Misiorowski, AL, NL Stat Leaders Ahead of 2026 MLB Season's Final Weekend
With five days remaining in the 2026 MLB regular season, the individual stats leaderboard is almost as unsettled as the playoff races in both leagues.
The key races going into the final weekend involve Yordan Alvarez's quest for the AL triple crown and Jacob Misiorowski looking to lead all of MLB in strikeouts.
Here are the leaders in several individual categories going into Wednesday's games.
TOP NEWS
Teams Scouting Cespedes' Son 🤯
Ranking MLB's 10 Greatest Postseason Runs Since 2000 🏆
Rays' Revamped Throwback Uni 🔥
| Category | American League | National League |
| Batting Average | Yordan Alvarez (Astros): .314 | Luis Arraez (Phillies): .314 |
| Home Runs | Alvarez (Astros) and Junior Caminero (Rays): 41 | Kyle Schwarber (Phillies) and Pete Crow-Armstrong (Cubs): 45 |
| RBI | Pete Alonso (Orioles): 108 | Alec Burleson (Cardinals): 111 |
| Hits | Yandy Diaz (Rays): 175 | Otto Lopez (Marlins): 186 |
| Stolen Bases | Chandler Simpson (Rays): 46 | Nasim Nunez (Nationals): 47 |
| Wins | Sonny Gray (Red Sox): 17 | Cristopher Sánchez (Phillies): 18 |
| Innings | Michael Wacha (Royals): 194.1 | Sandy Alcantara (Marlins): 212.0 |
| ERA | Cam Schlittler (Yankees): 1.94 | Jacob Misiorowski (Brewers): 1.86 |
| Strikeouts | Gavin Williams (Guardians): 244 | Jacob Misiorowski (Brewers): 247 |
| Saves | Bryan Baker (Rays) and Cade Smith (Guardians): 40 | Riley O'Brien (Cardinals): 38 |
Alvarez will need a strong close to the season to win the triple crown. He still leads the AL in average and is tied for the lead in homers, but his RBI pace has fallen off this month.
The Houston Astros star had just five RBI in his first 16 games in September before driving in three on Tuesday in a 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners.
Alvarez is up to 102 RBI for the season. Pete Alonso's 17 RBI this month have pushed him up to 108 with five games remaining.
Alvarez and Luis Arraez are tied for the MLB lead with a .314 batting average. Both players look like safe bets to maintain that position through Sunday.
Misiorowski, the biggest breakout star of the season for the 2026 NL Central champion Milwaukee Brewers, is looking to become the first pitcher to lead MLB in both ERA and strikeouts in a 162-game season since Jake Peavy in 2007.
The MLB ERA title is down to Misiorowski at 1.86 and New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler at 1.94. Misiorowski will likely get one more abbreviated start in Milwaukee's final regular-season series against the St. Louis Cardinals.
Schlittler is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Thursday against the Tampa Bay Rays. Since the Yankees are locked into the No. 4 seed, he is also likely to have a shortened outing to prepare for Game 1 of the wild-card round on Tuesday.
The strikeout race is arguably more compelling than the ERA title because Gavin Williams of the Cleveland Guardians will likely get the nod on Friday against the Kansas City Royals.
Since the Guardians can't wrap up the AL Central until Friday at the earliest, Williams will likely have a regular outing. He is currently only three Ks behind Misiorowski for the MLB lead.
Williams has 15 strikeouts in 11.2 innings against the Royals this season, but he hasn't faced them since May 5.
NL MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong is one stolen base away from the seventh player in MLB history to have a 40-40 season. He can also become the first Chicago Cubs player to lead the NL in homers since Sammy Sosa hit 49 in 2002.

Blue Jays Announce George Spri
item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays began a series with the Baltimore Orioles on Monday, dropping the opener 4-3.
Yet, Tuesday's game was postponed, setting up Wednesday for a doubleheader with the first game scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET.
Ahead of the matchup, Blue Jays manager John Schneider decided to keep his starting lineup relatively similar to Monday's as superstar Vladimir Guerrero Jr. misses his second straight game after exiting Sunday's contest with lower back tightness.
Blue Jays Announce George Springer Decision
While he's been in more of a platoon role this season for Toronto, Schneider is keeping Springer in the cleanup spot for Wednesday's game as he's once again slotted in as the designated hitter.
Across four at-bats on Monday, Springer recorded two hits and an RBI. He'll hit behind Kazuma Okamoto, Josh Smith, and Nathan Lukes, who will man the top three spots in the batting order, while Sean Keys takes over at first base for Guerrero Jr. and hits fifth.
Here's the full Blue Jays lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Blue Jays Game 1 9/23 N. Lukes RF J. Smith LF K. Okamoto 3B G. Springer DH S. Keys 1B A. Giménez SS B. Valenzuela C M. Straw CF E. Clement 2B M. Scherzer SP."
Blue Jays Game 1 9/23
N. Lukes RF
J. Smith LF
K. Okamoto 3B
G. Springer DH
S. Keys 1B
A. Giménez SS
B. Valenzuela C
M. Straw CF
E. Clement 2B
M. Scherzer SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 23, 2026
Springer's 2026 Season
In his 13th MLB season, Springer has had to take a step back in certain ways, most notably defensively, as he hardly plays the outfield anymore for Toronto.
But he still remains a highly productive player at the plate.
Appearing in 123 games for the Blue Jays this season, Springer enters Wednesday hitting .251 with 57 runs, 113 hits, 15 home runs, and 54 RBIs while slugging .408 with a .732 OPS.
Looking at the Blue Jays
At 77-80 overall, one loss would eliminate the Blue Jays from the playoff race, less than a year removed from reaching the World Series.
It's been an underwhelming season for Toronto. And as they sit 4.0 games back of the final Wild Card spot, it's likely they won't be playing in October this year barring a late-season miracle with five regular-season games remaining.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Toronto Blue Jays Announce George Springer Decision During Orioles Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
Por: Edgar Ochoa/ NOTIVER
Un veracruzano en el top de los catchers
Baseball America volvió a poner los reflectores sobre el talento mexicano al publicar su lista de los 10 mejores prospectos de nuestro país rumbo a las Grandes Ligas, encabezada por Christian Zazueta, seguido por Carlos Gutiérrez y el receptor Alberto Barriga, una muestra del enorme crecimiento que está teniendo el béisbol mexicano.
Ser considerado dentro de este grupo no solamente representa reconocimiento, sino también un enorme compromiso para estos jóvenes que están construyendo su camino hacia el mejor béisbol del mundo.
Gutiérrez, perteneciente a los Algodoneros de Guasave, fue firmado originalmente por San Francisco y durante 2026 pasó a la organización de los Red Sox de Boston.
Barriga, también de Guasave, forma parte de la organización de Arizona y se ha consolidado como uno de los receptores mexicanos con mayor proyección.
José Verdugo, originario de La Trinidad, Guasave, también aparece entre los destacados y pertenece a los Cañeros de Los Mochis.
Zazueta, por su parte, pertenece a los Mayos de Navojoa en la Liga Mexicana del Pacífico y a los Dodgers en MLB, donde su ascenso lo ha colocado entre los principales prospectos del béisbol.
Este tema lo platiqué con mi buen amigo Juan Carlos García Sampieri, porque coincidimos en que estar entre los mejores 10 prospectos mexicanos significa tener una gran oportunidad, pero también asumir una responsabilidad todavía mayor.
El futuro está ahí y ahora toca trabajar, aprender y demostrar que México tiene talento para rato.
Manuel Cazarín, una leyenda veracruzana
Y continuando con receptores jarochos.
El nombre de Manuel Cazarín está escrito con letras grandes en la historia del béisbol veracruzano y mexicano, un receptor nacido en Tlalixcoyan que durante 25 temporadas en la Liga Mexicana de Béisbol dejó constancia de su enorme calidad, entrega y amor por el juego.
Defendió las franelas de equipos históricos como El Águila de Veracruz, Petroleros de Minatitlán, Piratas de Campeche, Langosteros de Cancún, Bravos de León, Olmecas de Tabasco y Tigres de Quintana Roo, acumulando la impresionante cifra de 2,232 juegos disputados y demostrando una consistencia ofensiva que lo llevó a terminar su carrera con promedio de .280.
Cazarín también tuvo siete temporadas por encima de .300, además de conectar 2,134 imparables, 389 dobles y 166 cuadrangulares, impulsando 1,028 carreras.
En la Liga Mexicana del Pacífico jugó durante 16 temporadas y formó parte de aquel inolvidable campeonato de los Tomateros de Culiacán en 1996, coronándose posteriormente en la Serie del Caribe.
Su trayectoria habla de un pelotero completo, resistente y comprometido, de esos que entendían que detrás de cada batazo había que poner disciplina, carácter y corazón.
Hoy su nombre aparece entre los precandidatos al Salón de la Fama del Béisbol Mexicano, y para quienes conocimos y admiramos su carrera, ese reconocimiento representa un acto de justicia a una trayectoria extraordinaria.
Para mí, Manuel Cazarín merece estar entre los inmortales de nuestro béisbol y considero que es cuestión de tiempo para que su nombre quede definitivamente grabado en ese recinto, porque las grandes carreras no se olvidan y la del “Tigre de Tlalixcoyan”es, sin duda, una de ellas.
OHTANI ESTÁ DE REGRESO
Después de permanecer el tiempo mínimo en la lista de lesionados, Shohei Ohtani está listo para regresar este miércoles al line up de los Dodgers frente a los Padres en el Dodger Stadium, una noticia que ilusiona a Los Ángeles justo cuando quedan solamente cinco juegos de temporada regular.
El japonés volverá únicamente como bateador, mientras continúa fuera de acción como lanzador debido a las molestias en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda.
Antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados tenía 30 cuadrangulares y un OPS de .902, números que reflejan el peso que tiene su presencia en la ofensiva angelina.
Durante su recuperación trabajó con los coaches y utilizó la máquina Trajekt para enfrentar simulaciones de pitcheos reales y recuperar sensaciones en la caja de bateo.
Dave Roberts adelantó que Ohtani podría no aparecer como primer bate ante el zurdo Robbie Ray, pues los Dodgers analizan alternar la parte alta del orden dependiendo del brazo del pitcher rival.
Ante lanzadores derechos, Ohtani seguiría teniendo la posibilidad de encabezar el lineup, mientras que Mookie Betts podría ocupar ese lugar frente a zurdos.
El objetivo es claro: darle turnos al bate y ritmo competitivo antes de que llegue la postemporada, porque el fenómeno japonés está de vuelta y los Dodgers quieren tenerlo listo para octubre.

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] Chris Sale takes the mound for the Atlanta Braves
item.dc:creator: Sam Peebles
item.description: In what will likely be his last regular season start for the Atlanta Braves this season, Chris Sale will be facing off against Andrew Abbott and the Cincinnati Reds. Chris Sale is not the front runner for the Cy Young award, but will most certainly get some second and third place votes with his 2.18 ERA, 30.3 percent strikeout rate, and league leading strikeout to walk ratio of 6.13. item.content:encoded:
In what will likely be his last regular season start for the Atlanta Braves this season, Chris Sale will be facing off against Andrew Abbott and the Cincinnati Reds.
Chris Sale is not the front runner for the Cy Young award, but will most certainly get some second and third place votes with his 2.18 ERA, 30.3 percent strikeout rate, and league leading strikeout to walk ratio of 6.13. Sale also leads the NL is best HR rate of 0.5 per nine innings, and best walk rate in the NL of 4.9 percent.
Side note, Chris Sale has the best career strikeout to walk ratio of all-time. Sale has also pitched 157.0 innings thus far this season, which is hurting his Cy Young chances to guys like Jacob Misiorowski. It could be argued that he has passed his fellow competitor Cristopher Sánchez, but Sánchez has a whopping 200.0 IP which is second in MLB behind Sandy Alcantara.
The Braves got a scare yesterday when Ronald Acuña fouled a ball off his shin, but luckily all the tests came back negative. The Braves have already clinched the division so a loss to the Reds yesterday was not a huge deal except the chances of a playoff bye are quickly fading. The offense looked bad again, so hopefully they can catch a spark again before the playoffs take off.
No Braves player has faced Abbott more than five at-bats. Ha-Seong Kim has a HR in his four at-bats and Ozzie Albies has a .600 average. Michael Harris has struggled to an OPS of .400 in his five at-bats, and Mauricio Dubón and Mike Yastrzemski are hitless in their three at-bats. Austin Riley is also hitless in five at-bats.
It is hard to make any type of prediction on such a limited history, but we can look at Abbott's numbers and see his 4.70 ERA is approximately eleven percent below average and his 1.472 WHIP is the worst of his four year career. This season he has struggled with walks giving up 4.2 per nine innings. The Braves need to be patient this even and take advantage of his weakness. It is no secret that the Braves struggle in the walk department. Their 7.7 percent is the third worst in MLB. To be fair, they strike out at a lower rate than the average team this season, but walks get runners on base to knock in.
The Reds are in the bottom six in RP ERA this season. The Braves have feasted on RPs all season long. The key to the game tonight seems to be be patient against Abbott because he gives up a lot of walks. Get to the bullpen, and strike. Chris Sale should keep the runs low to make this a pretty easy win on paper. The question is how many players will be resting today, especially with a high likelihood that Acuña will be letting his leg heal.
First pitch is at 7:15 EDT.
Game Info
Game Time: Wednesday, September 23rd, 7:15 pm EDT
Location: Truist Park, Atlanta, GA
Watch: BravesVision
Radio/Audio: 680 AM / 93.7 FM The Fan

item.content:encoded:
The Houston Astros have endured an unusually inconsistent 2026 MLB season, but remain firmly in playoff contention as the final week of the regular season continues.
Houston enters Wednesday’s matchup with the Seattle Mariners at 78-79, tied for first place in the American League West with the Texas Rangers. Although the Astros have lost seven of their last ten games and remain below .500, they still find themselves fighting for a division title with just five games to go.
No player has done more to keep the Astros in the playoff race than Yordan Alvarez. After a 2025 season that was plagued by injuries, Alvarez has bounced back in 2026, putting together the best regular season of his career.
A Career Year in Houston
The four-time All-Star is slashing .314/.431/.601, adding 41 home runs and 102 RBIs through 153 games. His 1.033 OPS is the best in baseball this season, and he is tied with Junior Caminero for the most home runs in the American League.
Alvarez has continued to come through while the Astros fight for the division lead. Tuesday against the Mariners, he homered and drove in three runs in a 7-0 victory that helped the Astros pull back into a tie in the division with the Rangers.
For Alvarez, his combination of production, power, and respect from opposing managers has placed him in rare historical company.
Baseball Royalty
According to Francys Romero, Alvarez is “now just the 5th player in MLB with 40+ HR, 100+ RBI and 30+ intentional walks in a single season before turning 30.”
The only other players to accomplish the feat are Albert Pujols, Ryan Howard, Barry Bonds and Kevin Mitchell. Pujols was the most recent, doing so during the 2009 season with the St. Louis Cardinals.
Joining this elite company shines a light on just how dominant Alvarez’s season has been, and how crucial he has been in keeping the team’s season alive.
Still fighting for the AL West crown, the Astros will need Alvarez to maintain his MVP-caliber production if the team hopes to secure a postseason spot and make a run in October.

item.title: [Infobae] Jonathan Aranda y los Tampa Bay Rays aseguran el liderato de División rumbo a los playoffs de la MLB
item.dc:creator: Luis Mote Nava
item.description: Los Tampa Bay Rays, equipo del mexicano Jonathan Aranda, aseguraron el liderato de la División Este de la Liga Americana tras vencer 6-1 a los New York Yankees en el segundo juego de la doble cartelera disputada este martes por la noche en el Bronx. El conjunto de Florida conquista el título divisional por primera vez desde 2021 y buscará trasladar el nivel mostrado durante la temporada regular a los playoffs. PUBLICIDAD Jonathan Aranda mantiene una temporada de alto nivel con los Rays Jonathan
item.content:encoded:
Los Tampa Bay Rays, equipo del mexicano Jonathan Aranda, aseguraron el liderato de la División Este de la Liga Americana tras vencer 6-1 a los New York Yankees en el segundo juego de la doble cartelera disputada este martes por la noche en el Bronx.
El conjunto de Florida conquista el título divisional por primera vez desde 2021 y buscará trasladar el nivel mostrado durante la temporada regular a los playoffs.
PUBLICIDAD
Jonathan Aranda mantiene una temporada de alto nivel con los Rays
Jonathan Aranda sostiene una temporada destacada con los Tampa Bay Rays y se consolida como uno de los bateadores de contacto más constantes tanto del equipo como de las Grandes Ligas.
El mexicano ocupa el sexto lugar de la Liga Americana en imparables, con 157. También suma 22 cuadrangulares y 92 carreras impulsadas, cifra que lo coloca entre los seis mejores productores de carreras del circuito.
Su camino hacia MLB comenzó hace poco más de una década, cuando fue firmado desde la Academia de Toros de Tijuana. A partir de entonces recorrió el sistema de sucursales hasta llegar al primer equipo de Tampa Bay en 2022.
PUBLICIDAD
La gran temporada de los Rays y su camino en los playoffs
Los Tampa Bay Rays han tenido una temporada regular consistente que les aseguró un lugar en la postemporada. El equipo mantiene una marca de 96-61, la mejor de la Liga Americana, con cinco juegos todavía por disputar.
Con ese desempeño, Tampa Bay aseguró el descanso durante la ronda de comodines y avanzó de manera directa a la siguiente fase. Ahora espera conocer a su rival en la Serie Divisional.
De mantenerse las posiciones en la recta final del calendario, los New York Yankees y los Boston Red Sox se enfrentarían en la ronda de comodines por el pase ante los Rays. El panorama aún podría modificarse en los últimos juegos de la campaña regular.
PUBLICIDAD
Si Boston atraviesa una mala racha, Chicago White Sox podría alcanzarlo en la clasificación, pues se encuentra a tres juegos de los Red Sox con cinco juegos por delante.
En ese escenario, los White Sox también surgirían como posibles rivales de Tampa Bay en la postemporada.
Cómo marcha el panorama de cara a la postemporada en las demás divisiones
Los New York Yankees y los Boston Red Sox ya aseguraron su lugar en la postemporada como equipos comodín. Aun así, Boston podría pasar del segundo al tercer puesto de la clasificación, dependiendo de los resultados en la recta final de la temporada.
Los Chicago White Sox mantienen, por ahora, el último boleto disponible a los playoffs. Sin embargo, todavía tienen presión de otros equipos que buscan alcanzarlos: los Texas Rangers se encuentran a tres juegos, mientras que los Toronto Blue Jays y los Baltimore Orioles permanecen más rezagados, a cinco victorias de distancia.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, el equipo de la Ciudad de los Vientos todavía aspira a ser campeón de la División Central de la Liga Americana, los Cleveland Guardians conservan una ventaja de apenas un juego, por lo que todavía no tienen asegurado el primer lugar.
La lucha por el título de la División Oeste de la Liga Americana también se mantiene abierta. Los Houston Astros y los Texas Rangers tienen el mismo récord, por lo que el campeón divisional se definirá en los últimos juegos del calendario regular.
Pasando a la Liga Nacional, la disputa se concentra en los puestos de comodín, ya que las divisiones tendrían definidos a sus líderes. Los Atlanta Braves encabezan el Este y los Milwaukee Brewers dominan la Central, mientras que los Dodgers nuevamente se adueñaron del Oeste.
PUBLICIDAD
La carrera por los boletos de comodín en la Nacional es más compacta, pues solamente hay cuatro equipos para tres boletos con Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies y San Diego Padres compartiendo récord de 87-70, mientras que los Arizona Diamondbacks se mantienen a cuatro juegos de distancia en la pelea por alcanzar la postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Marcus Semien Remembers Rangers Fondly Even After Trade to Mets
item.dc:creator: Matt Postins; Unknown
item.description: Marcus Semien acknowledges that his final two seasons in Texas were rough statistically, but it doesn't dampen how he feels about the franchise and what he accomplished. The second baseman was back in Globe Life Field for the first time since he was traded in the offseason. The Rangers dealt Semien, who signed a seven-year deal with the organization before the 2022 season, to the New York Mets for outfielder Brandon Nimmo. To many, he's still the second baseman that slammed home runs in both Gam
item.content:encoded:
Marcus Semien acknowledges that his final two seasons in Texas were rough statistically, but it doesn't dampen how he feels about the franchise and what he accomplished.
The second baseman was back in Globe Life Field for the first time since he was traded in the offseason. The Rangers dealt Semien, who signed a seven-year deal with the organization before the 2022 season, to the New York Mets for outfielder Brandon Nimmo.
To many, he's still the second baseman that slammed home runs in both Game 4 and Game 5 of the 2023 World Series as he helped deliver the organization's first championship after more than 50 years of waiting. He called it the “pinnacle” of his career, in a conversation with reporters, including Shawn McFarland of The Dallas Morning News (subscription required).
"We really had a great group of guys in that clubhouse," Semien said. "[Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young], that was his goal, was to bring the right people in. It all worked out."
Marcus Semien and The Rangers
When Semien arrived in Texas, he was coming off a career offensive season with the Toronto Blue Jays in 2021, during which he batted .265 and hit a career best 45 home runs and 102 RBI. He had also developed a reputation as an iron man. That season he played 162 games for the second straight year. He continued that in Texas.
He struggled coming out of the gate in his first season in Texas, which featured a truncated spring training due to a work stoppage. He finished with a slash of .248/.304/.429 with 26 home runs and 83 RBI as his season was energized by being moved to the leadoff spot.
Slow starts would be a fixture for Semien throughout his time in Texas, but in 2023 he had the best all-around season of his career. He played all 162 games and slashed .276/.348/.478 with 29 home runs and 100 RBI. He was voted the starter for the American League in the All-Star Game, won an AL Silver Slugger and was third in AL MVP voting behind Shohei Ohtani and his teammate, Corey Seager.
His last two seasons saw a decline in production and a foot injury that ended his season prematurely last August. He slashed .234/.307/.379 with 38 home runs and 136 RBI in 2024 and 2025 as he dropped out of the leadoff spot. He was named an All-Star in 2024 and won an AL Gold Glove in 2025 even with the injury.
He missed time with an injury with the Mets earlier this year and he’s struggled with his bat again, as he slashed .219/.285/.341 with 14 home runs and 48 RBI. He has two years remaining on his deal.
Semien still lives in the Dallas area, even after the trade. It appears he not only found a title in Texas, but he found a home.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Cubs' Alex Bregman pushing for regular-season return after foul ball injury
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: CHICAGO — Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman could play again in the regular season after he sustained multiple facial fractures when he was struck in the face by a foul ball.
