item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- Ronald Acuña Jr. was forced to exit Tuesday night’s game against the Reds at Truist Park after fouling a pitch off his lower left leg in the bottom of the third inning. The Braves later announced he had suffered a left shin contusion, but that X-rays were negative.
Acuña fell to the ground in pain immediately after the foul ball hit just between his left shin guard and left knee. He tried to take a few steps before going to the ground again.
The Braves' outfielder was able to get to the dugout under his own power.
Acuña entered Tuesday tied with Alex Bregman for MLB’s second-best OPS (1.119) dating back to Aug. 28.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber Are Key to Phillies Playoff Success
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Teape; Unknown
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies have a little bit of work left to do to secure a playoff spot in the National League. With six games remaining in the regular season, the Phillies hold a four-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks. But because they do not possess the tiebreaker, Philadelphia still has a Magic Number of three. Over the next six games, they need some combination of three victories of their own and losses by the Diamondbacks. They are heavily favored to make the postseason field, but the
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies have a little bit of work left to do to secure a playoff spot in the National League.
With six games remaining in the regular season, the Phillies hold a four-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks. But because they do not possess the tiebreaker, Philadelphia still has a Magic Number of three.
Over the next six games, they need some combination of three victories of their own and losses by the Diamondbacks. They are heavily favored to make the postseason field, but then will be jostling for seeding with the Chicago Cubs, who are currently the No. 1 Wild Card team, and the San Diego Padres, who are currently No. 2.
To catch those teams and make any noise in the playoffs, the Phillies are going to need their stars to play up to their capabilities. Two players they will be counting on to produce are right fielder Bryce Harper and designated hitter Kyle Schwarber.
Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber have been elite against fastballs
In the playoffs, there is a little extra juice when facing opponents. Pitchers are throwing the ball a little harder, and handling velocity becomes a key component for a team to find success. Luckily for Philadelphia, their two star sluggers are among the best in baseball when facing heat.
Some of the nastiest offerings in baseball are off-speed and breaking pitches that can play up a four-seam fastball. So, when a batter gets the opportunity to jump one of those fastballs, they need to make it count.
Harper and Schwarber both accomplish that. As shared by David Adler of MLB.com, thus far in 2026, they are two of the most productive players in the MLB against fastballs. Schwarber is second in the MLB with a batting run value of +30 runs created, which trails only Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros, who has +32.
The Phillies slugger has launched 27 home runs against fastballs this season, which is the most in the MLB. Harper has hit 18 home runs when facing fastballs, and his +28 runs created is the third most in baseball. Willson Contreras of the Boston Red Sox and Ben Rice of the New York Yankees round out the top five with +25 and +23 runs created apiece.
Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber produce under brightest lights
While the Philadelphia duo has succeeded against that pitch type, they have also gotten the job done even when the pitcher is throwing with elite velocity. When facing fastballs that are 97 mph or faster this season, Harper has a slugging percentage of .523 with three long balls.
Schwarber has been slightly better, with a .525 slugging percentage and six home runs, which once again leads the MLB.
Even more encouraging for the Phillies is that since the two became teammates, their production against fastballs is even better in the playoffs. Harper has an eye-popping .778 slugging percentage with eight home runs since 2022, making him the best fastball hitter in the MLB postseason during that span.
Schwarber has 10 home runs in the playoffs with a .722 slugging percentage. Hopefully, they keep that production up to help Philadelphia advance in the postseason.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Zack Wheeler opens with Phillies record 7 straight strikeouts, hits 2,000 for career
item.dc:creator: Kristie Ackert; USA TODAY
item.description: Zack Wheeler walked out to the mound at Citizens Bank Park Tuesday night needing three strikeouts to reach 2,000. It took him 12 pitches. Garrett Mitchell went down first. Then Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang were rung up as Wheeler reached the milestone against the Milwaukee Brewers. But, Wheeler kept going. William Contreras, Jake Bauers and Christian Yelich struck out in the second. Luis Lara struck out to lead off the third inning. Wheeler struck out seven straight Brewers to start the game
item.content:encoded:
Zack Wheeler walked out to the mound at Citizens Bank Park Tuesday night needing three strikeouts to reach 2,000. It took him 12 pitches. Garrett Mitchell went down first. Then Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang were rung up as Wheeler reached the milestone against the Milwaukee Brewers.
But, Wheeler kept going.
William Contreras, Jake Bauers and Christian Yelich struck out in the second. Luis Lara struck out to lead off the third inning. Wheeler struck out seven straight Brewers to start the game, something no Phillies pitcher had done to start a game. Cooper Pratt finally ended it by grounding out to third.
Wheeler, 36, is the 96th pitcher in major league history to reach 2,000 strikeouts and only nine got there faster.
It came almost a year after a surgeon in St. Louis removed his top rib to address the circulation problem in his arm.
The trouble started after a start in Washington on Aug. 15, 2025. Wheeler felt some heaviness in his right shoulder. By the next morning doctors had found a blood clot near it. The diagnosis was venous thoracic outlet syndrome, meaning a vein was getting pinched between his collarbone and rib cage. The fix was taking out the first rib and some of the muscle around it. He missed the rest of the season and the playoffs.
He came back April 25 against Atlanta, capped at 90 pitches. He hasn't looked back. Wheeler entered Tuesday 13-5 with a 2.99 ERA and 177 strikeouts in 150½ innings. In his previous four starts he had allowed three runs in 26 innings.
Aaron Nola still owns the Phillies' mark for strikeouts in a row at any point in a game. He struck out 10 straight Mets in June 2021, matching Tom Seaver's major league record from 1970. The modern record for starting a game that way is nine, set by Miami's Pablo Lopez against Atlanta in 2021.
Wheeler finished with 11 strikeouts Tuesday night in 5⅔ innings.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Zack Wheeler opens with Phillies record 7 straight strikeouts, hits 2,000 for career

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Alex Bregman injury update shows how he has changed the Chicago Cubs
item.dc:creator: Gavin Groe
item.description: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman suffered multiple fractures in his face after being struck inadvertently by a foul ball this past Sunday during a game against the Cincinnati Reds. The injury occurred in the top of the fourth inning while Bregman was standing in the on-deck circle. Cubs first baseman Michael Busch checked his swing and the ball immediately struck Bregman. He was removed from the game and hospitalized as he underwent imaging to confirm the severity of his injuries. Bregman
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman suffered multiple fractures in his face after being struck inadvertently by a foul ball this past Sunday during a game against the Cincinnati Reds. The injury occurred in the top of the fourth inning while Bregman was standing in the on-deck circle. Cubs first baseman Michael Busch checked his swing and the ball immediately struck Bregman.
He was removed from the game and hospitalized as he underwent imaging to confirm the severity of his injuries. Bregman also shared graphic images of the injury which worried Cubs fans given how swollen his face was and how close the MLB postseason is.
However, manager Craig Counsell had an encouraging update when speaking with reporters ahead of Tuesday's game against the Miami Marlins.
Counsell shared that not only would Bregman avoid the injured list entirely, but there is a chance he even returns before the end of the regular season. He even took part in strength work and tracked pitches from a machine, officially resuming baseball activities.
What Alex Bregman Has Meant to the Chicago Cubs
Bregman's decision to push through the discomfort speaks volumes about his character and what he has brought to this Cubs team. Bregman signed this past offseason to a five-year, $175 million deal, which was quite the investment for an aging infielder whose prime may be behind him. However, one of the main reasons Chicago made the move was for his veteran presence and ability to lead by example.
Everywhere Bregman has played in his career, teams win. In Houston he won a World Series title, and with the Red Sox last year he helped take them to the MLB playoffs, guiding a young team not just with his bat but with his toughness and leadership.
National League MVP frontrunner Pete Crow-Armstrong has even credited Bregman for his success this year and for being in his corner throughout the season.
Sep 18, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman (3) waits on deck to bat before the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
For the Cubs, Bregman being available will improve their playoff chances on the field. But his addition to the clubhouse in general has been invaluable. The Cubs are on the verge of punching their ticket to the postseason, and Bregman will be along for the ride.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Blue Jays Receive Encouraging News About Dylan Cease's Injury
item.dc:creator: Maanav Gupta; Unknown
item.description: Injuries have started to take a toll on the Toronto Blue Jays lately. While it seemed like there was still hope for Toronto to make the postseason a couple of weeks ago, that has ultimately not turned out to be the case. The struggles have been real, and the injuries have not made it easier. Outfielder Brett Bateman suffered a hip injury on Monday night, while first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has dealt with back tightness. Not to mention starter Trey Yesavage, who just returned from knee surg
item.content:encoded:
Injuries have started to take a toll on the Toronto Blue Jays lately. While it seemed like there was still hope for Toronto to make the postseason a couple of weeks ago, that has ultimately not turned out to be the case.
The struggles have been real, and the injuries have not made it easier. Outfielder Brett Bateman suffered a hip injury on Monday night, while first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has dealt with back tightness. Not to mention starter Trey Yesavage, who just returned from knee surgery after six weeks.
Ace Dylan Cease had been holding down the rotation recently, but even he hasn't been immune to the injury bug that has hurt the Blue Jays this season. Cease has been a lifeline to Toronto's pitching staff, but had been dealing with shoulder fatigue over the past few weeks, according to manager John Schneider.
Cease struggled mightily against the Texas Rangers on Friday, going just 2.2 innings and walking six, while giving up four runs (one earned). He went back to Toronto for an MRI and was scratched from his next start on Wednesday.
It was revealed on Monday that the MRI only showed inflammation in the right shoulder and no structural issues. Cease will not need surgery for anything more serious.
More on Cease's Injury Situation
The 30-year-old explained the news himself and the fact that he's just been diagnosed with shoulder inflammation. This isn't an issue that is expected to go into 2027 and affect his availability for next season.
It's still unlikely that Cease ends up pitching again this season with less than a week left, although that's still being determined. Given the Jays are basically out of postseason contention, there's really no need to push him.
The shoulder issue is what caused Cease's pitch velocity to go down.
“The velocity being down has been a little bit concerning,” Cease said, according to Keegan Matheson of MLB.com. "But at the same time, I’m getting outs. It wasn’t anything that was too scary because nothing about it feels like I’ve got something that needs surgery."
After his incredible complete game at the Boston Red Sox on July 25, where he threw 120 pitches, Cease didn't look as strong, even though he still ended up throwing six quality starts from that time until now.
“It’s definitely a bit heavy and achy, just not normal,” Cease said. "The last couple of starts, the velo keeps going down and down. Especially that last one, I almost felt like I was hurting the team."
It's clear that the issue caught him to him, but the fact that he pitched through it at a high level for some time shows the quality of Cease.
He has posted a 2.40 ERA in 29 starts, which is the second-lowest mark in the American League. Cease has a career-high 239 strikeouts in 169 innings pitched, with an 11-6 record.
Maanav Gupta primarily covers Houston sports for On SI. He graduated from the University of Houston in the summer of 2025 with his bachelor’s in journalism and a minor in Spanish. Gupta spent three years at the student newspaper, The Daily Cougar, and also covered the 2025 Final Four and National Championship. He also has his own YouTube channel, Maanav’s Sports Talk, where he has interviewed professional athletes and broadcasters like Jose Altuve, Jeremy Peña, J.J. Watt, and Jim Nantz. Gupta has been writing about the Astros for various publications since 2024. You can find Gupta on X, Instagram and TikTok @MGSportsTalk.

item.title: [phillyvoice.com] The Phillies aren't serious
item.dc:creator: Nick Tricome PhillyVoice Staff
item.description: September 22, 2026 The Phillies gave Saturday away, then gave themselves a golden chance to take it back. But in almost textbook Philadelphia Phillies fashion, they let it go. Brooks Raley loaded the bases in relief of Andrew Painter one out into the bottom of the sixth, and with a one-run lead, then gave up a Brett Baty liner into center that a diving Justin Crawford could only trap between his glove and the grass for another Mets run scored – and with the bases still full. item.content:encoded:
September 22, 2026
The Phillies gave Saturday away, then gave themselves a golden chance to take it back.
But in almost textbook Philadelphia Phillies fashion, they let it go.
Brooks Raley loaded the bases in relief of Andrew Painter one out into the bottom of the sixth, and with a one-run lead, then gave up a Brett Baty liner into center that a diving Justin Crawford could only trap between his glove and the grass for another Mets run scored – and with the bases still full.
Interim manager Don Mattingly yanked Raley as soon as he could for Chase Shugart, and he walked in another to Ronny Mauricio – a .173 hitter at the bottom of the New York order – before a warning-track flyout from Francisco Lindor mercifully ended the frame.
The Phillies set themselves up with a bases-loaded answer of their own in the top of the seventh, after Trea Turner and Alec Bohm drew walks and Luis Arráez singled around a Kyle Schwarber groundout and a Bryce Harper strikeout. But under the pressure situation, Bryson Stott hacked a roller through the grass to second and was left slamming his helmet into the dirt as the Mets jogged back to their dugout without any damage.
The night unraveled from there. The Phillies lost to the Mets, 10-3, up in Queens. Orion Kerkering got tagged for the second straight game, letting up four more runs in the eighth, then was demoted to Triple-A after in a move that essentially exiles the struggling reliever from the roster.
They came back with a 7-2 win the next day, behind a stellar outing from ace Cristopher Sánchez that salvaged a 2-2 split in a four-game series, but with the whole weekend taken into account, it wasn't any kind of silver lining.
The Phillies are supposed to be a playoff team, and still more than likely will be, but they had four games against a Mets club living in the NL East basement right there for the taking. It was the schedule's last gimme. And yet they couldn't help but throw two of those games down the gutter, for little other reason than that they couldn't get out of their own way.
The Phillies were supposed to, or at least wanted fans to think, that they turned over a new leaf at the plate, hitting through August with the kind of small ball approach that their power-heavy lineup went out of its way to avoid for way too long, but they've since reverted back to the old habits and stubborn cold streaks that have long overstayed their welcome.
And the Phillies were supposed to have, or rather praying for, a somewhat stable bullpen after the trade deadline, but now it's so fickle and with so little time left that decisions seem destined to come down to "what starter moves into the bullpen for the postseason?"
It's been this way for five years now, through many big-money contracts that feel like they're never quite living up to the price tag, through many more failed looks at bargain-bin arms, two (and what's looking on track to be three) managerial changes, a dramatic infield shuffle mid-season, and increasingly suspect prospect development that begs an increasingly scarier question of what kind of long-term future does this club really have?
The Phillies aren't a serious baseball team. Not anymore, at least.
They're still good, sure, in the sense that they can – and again, more than likely will – qualify for a spot in October.
But really, they could've locked that spot up a week ago.
Instead, they're 8-10 through September. They punted any possible shot at the NL East title out the window once they let the Braves go 4-3 against them across their final two series, and left a Diamondbacks club that has notoriously broken their hearts before with a faint (and therefore dangerous) glimmer of hope in the final NL Wild Card chase, while leaving a best-of-three road playoff series in Atlanta as the expected prize.
And oh yeah, they do still have to play two good teams that can easily exhaust and bury them before the Phils can even think about any of what might come after.
So where really is the contender in all of this?
Certainly the Phillies are going to lean on their elite starters between Sánchez, Zack Wheeler, a revitalized Aaron Nola, and Jesús Luzardo if they can get him back in time, but at the same time, that wasn't enough against the Mets in the 2024 NLDS or the Dodgers in the 2025 division series a year later. They each countered with shutdown pitching on their side, and hung in there until the Phillies inevitably had to reach into their volatile bullpen to capitalize.
And nothing about the 2026 club suggests that this time would be any different; not when Braves and Dodgers can continue to match them beat for beat talent-wise, while having already proved that they both play much smarter games – in the field, at the plate, and even more so on the base paths – and definitely not after they just showed that they're apparently not that much further above the lowly Mets.
Brandon Marsh, who had an All-Star first half, has one extra-base hit this month.
J.T. Realmuto, once labeled the best catcher in baseball, struck out six times in the Mets series and is a .213 hitter in his mid-30s.
Luis Arráez, who has batted well above .300 for years, suddenly dipped to a .285 average as a Phillie, and while Alec Bohm is impressing with a .328 average through the month, he's never going to hit with the power many hoped for out of a former first-round draft pick at a listed 6'4" and isn't going to suddenly discover it now at age 30 while heading toward free agency.
That leaves Harper and Schwarber as the star sluggers, but at this point, as bats who can be managed around or even directly challenged, while Turner seems to perpetually volley between a $300 million force one minute and a guy who looks like he forgot how to play shortstop the next.
Here's the catch, too: the above names are either in their late 20s at their youngest or pushing well into their 30s on average, after repeated years of trying and failing to out-thump the competition, and with not many more shots expected to be left, especially now that a labor strike puts a serious threat over 2027.
The Phils had a great August, but that was always with a tough September schedule looming, which was always going to tell you what kind of team they really were.
And while there are still six games left, and a probable postseason clinch, there's enough of a picture to tell you this: The Phillies aren't serious.
They haven't been, and really, unless something way more drastic happened at the deadline or Crawford or Painter instantly became the new faces of the franchise, that reality was staring everyone in the face all winter – when the only noticeable difference to the lineup was that Nick Castellanos wasn't in it anymore.
Are they still good enough for October? To get there, sure...probably...hopefully, after this week?
But any further than that? No. They haven't shown anything to say otherwise, or that they're any different from the last two Phillies clubs that hit a hard stop.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox might've cemented Craig Breslow’s rise off the hot seat too soon
item.dc:creator: Brian Burrows
item.description: The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years. With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. item.content:encoded:
The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years.
With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head of baseball operations who got his team to the playoffs in years two and three of their time running the club getting years added to their contract, would make sense, but in Breslow's case it isn't as straightforward.
It was only three months ago when most of Red Sox Nation was calling for Breslow's head. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24, dead last in the division, and it already seemed like the season was over. It took a miraculous turnaround to get the team to the playoffs. Not to say that Breslow had nothing to do with that; he had added a lot of players to the roster who were key contributors, but that has a lot more to do with the players and coaches than the front office.
Breslow's tenure has also been marred by controversy, specifically the Rafael Devers drama. It was his handling of the situation, along with former manager Alex Cora, that ultimately led to the fracture of the relationship with the team's then-face of the franchise. While the fanbase was split on whose side they took, player or team, his actions after the fact didn't make it any better.
Red Sox's Craig Breslow had the hottest seat of any GM only three months ago
It was the signing of Alex Bregman that caused the Devers drama in the first place. While Breslow was praised for the signing, Bregman opted out at the end of the year and was then not re-signed. The Red Sox went from two elite third basemen to none in the span of a season. It wasn't a good look for the Red Sox CBO.
Now, Breslow's pivot from all of the drama and mess surrounding Devers and Bregman looks incredibly good in hindsight. The additions of Ranger Suarez, Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and others have been extremely impactful to the Red Sox's success this season. While some of those moves were celebrated at the time they happened, others like the Durbin-Kyle Harrison swap (that also netted the Red Sox Andruw Monasterio and Anthony Seigler) were heavily scrutinized.
Breslow also made good moves at the trade deadline, adding Erik Miller and Eli White, who have looked good for the Sox. He also made the splash trade for Adley Rutschman, which hasn't worked as well on the field, but certainly instilled confidence in the team, knowing the front office believed in them.
Red Sox could've softened the impact by extending one of Craig Breslow's options at first
All of this is to say that Breslow's time as CBO hasn't been as smooth sailing as the records would suggest. He has had some high highs but also some low lows. Why did ownership feel the need to exercise both options right now? The first option wasn't needed until the 2029 season, two years out. The second was for 2030, three years out.
Doing the first one now would've been fine — picking up the 2029 option gives Breslow another three comfortable seasons on his contract. That would make him more comfortable making moves for the future and give him the job security to know he will likely be in place to see them play out. Selecting the 2030 option on the same day was unnecessary, though.
There have been too many hiccups in the three years under Breslow to say he has warranted another four seasons. The start of 2026 could easily repeat itself in 2027. Should ownership feel the need to relieve him of his duties early, then this makes it that much harder. Breslow hasn't won a World Series in Boston; in fact, he hasn't even made it out of the Wild Card round. Exercising the option for 2030 feels very premature.
Breslow has not done a bad job in Boston. At the end of the day, it's results that matter, and Breslow's teams have made the playoffs two out of three times. He shouldn't be fearing for his job, but his contract also wasn't ending for another two seasons. It feels early to be handing him the keys so far down the road after the drama of his first two years as CBO.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees win first game of doubleheader behind Carlos Rodón’s milestone performance
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of
item.content:encoded:
The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of the day’s doubleheader, 2-0.
Rodón burst out of the gate like he had a point to prove, whiffing the first two batters of the game Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda on a pair of filthy sliders. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are likely locks for the postseason rotation, meaning if the Yankees elect to stick with a three-man unit, that final spot comes down to Rodón and Gerrit Cole. Aaron Boone has affirmed his commitment to Cole as the Game One starter in a prospective Wild Card Series. This seemingly leaves Rodón on the bubble, which might explain the extra edge he was pitching with this afternoon.
His teammates didn’t do themselves any favors early, burning both ABS challenges in the first inning. I expect the Yankees to tighten the strings on who gets to challenge and in what situation come the playoffs as you cannot deprive yourself of such a vital tool with eight innings still to play.
Martinez entered this game with the lowest walk rate of any qualified starter and among the league’s best at limiting hard contact. He was true to form going the first turn through the order without allowing a base runner. He was helped by the collectively poor approach from the lineup, with four out of the nine batters including the side in the third striking out against a pitcher with the lowest strikeout rate among qualified starters.
That started to change the second turn through the order, the Yankees finally starting to do some damage against the high volume of pitches Martinez was throwing over the heart of the plate, starting with a Ben Rice double into the corner in right to lead off the fourth. The very next pitch Martinez threw rocketed out of the yard, Cody Bellinger blasting a first pitch sinker into the seats in right for a two-run homer — his fifth homer in the last 12 games.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones singled with two outs to put runners on the corners. Jones then stole second unopposed, but Anthony Volpe struck out swinging to strand the pair in scoring position. They kept up the pressure in the fifth, José Caballero reaching on a bunt single against his former team and then stealing second and third followed by a Rice walk to put runners on the corners with one out. However, Bellinger popped out and Heliot Ramos flew out as they stranded a pair in consecutive frames.
Rodón settled into an impressive groove after a Chandler Simpson single in the second, retiring the next ten batters in order until Victor Mesa Jr. led off the sixth with a single. After Rodón whiffed Jorge Mateo on a slider for his sixth strikeout, he got Richie Palacios to line out to left. Mesa was running on the play and momentarily forget he had to sprint back to first, allowing Bellinger to throw an absolute seed to Luis García Jr., who applid the tag for the inning-ending double play.
With Rodón’s pitch count standing at just 89 after seven, Boone decided to go batter-to-batter in the eighth. However, Rodón ensured his manager had no choice to make, completing the eighth inning on just seven pitches, including the 1,500th strikeout of his career. It’s tied for his longest start as a Yankee, matching the eight innings he pitched against the Cubs on July 11, 2025.
Rodón entered this start as perhaps the Yankees’ most in-form pitcher behind Schlittler. Including today, in his last eight starts, Rodón has a 1.67 ERA while holding batters to a measly .134 batting average against. He had all his pitches working today, but this really felt like a throwback to his peak years with Chicago and San Francisco. He got whiffs in bunches on the four-seamer above the zone and slider below it. In likely his penultimate start of the regular season, Rodón dominated for eight scoreless innings, allowing three hits and no walks while striking out eight to lower his ERA to 2.67 on the year.
The Yankees didn’t manage another base runner in the final three innings, but Rodón made sure that it wouldn’t come back to haunt them. David Bednar pitched a one-two-three ninth to secure his 35th save of the season. The gap to the Rays now stands at five games as the Yankees become the second team in the AL to 90 wins. At worst, they have clinched the four seed in the AL, guaranteeing home field advantage in a prospective AL Wild Card Series.
The Yankees have a few hours’ rest before taking the field again tonight. Max Fried starts the night game of the doubleheader against Drew Rasmussen. First pitch is scheduled for 7:05 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES, so stick around!

item.title: [si.com] Samuel Basallo's Second Half Raises More Red Flags For Orioles Hitting Staff And Medical Staff
item.dc:creator: Jason La Canfora; Unknown
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles, under failed head of baseball operations Mike Elias, are incapable of cultivating their greatest resources into consistently productive players. Since running off one of the most respected and accomplished training staffs so Elias could bring in his own people, their Injured List stints have soared and the same recurring injuries have cropped up and their most important young everyday players have regressed, markedly and quickly, and, in some cases, perhaps permanently. So
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Orioles, under failed head of baseball operations Mike Elias, are incapable of cultivating their greatest resources into consistently productive players.
Since running off one of the most respected and accomplished training staffs so Elias could bring in his own people, their Injured List stints have soared and the same recurring injuries have cropped up and their most important young everyday players have regressed, markedly and quickly, and, in some cases, perhaps permanently. So watching 22-year-old catcher Samuel Basallo struggle mightily and not look like himself and appear to be compensating for a lingering shoulder injury deep into a lost season is a major concern for him (especially against the backdrop of what has become of Gunnar Henderson and Jackson Holliday, among others).
Wasn’t that long ago that Basallo was the most prodigious power hitting catcher under the age of 22 in MLB history, as we documented at the time. He also left a game against Toronto briefly back in May wincing and leaving with trainers, only to pop back up in the on deck circle late in the game, only to experience more issues that clownish rookie manager Craig Albernaz tried to minimize,only to end up on the IL in July, after all, with what was deemed “right shoulder inflammation” and struggle mightily ever since.
Carrying three catchers for most of the second half of the season, again, in a lost season, there seemed to be a mounting case for shutting down a young man who ended up catching infinitely more innings for this team than alleged star Adley Rutschman and endured his fair share of adversity in a rookie season at a very young age for someone manning this position. That seemed smart ever before he took a foul tip tot he head Monday that had him getting checked for a concussion.
It seems even more obvious, now.
This kid barely caught 200 games in the minors, and I am thoroughly convinced the shoulder situation has been fairly significant for way longer than they got around to putting him on the IL. Regardless, the second half has been a mess.
Hitting The Wall
Basallo has not seemed comfortable at all since being reactivated and his power stroke is lacking and he’s been getting under the ball a lot and failing to line things up. His strikeout rate has gone from 26% to 30%.
Split G GS PA HR RBI BA OBP SLG OPS
1st Half 83 70 301 16 46 .248 .309 .464 .772
2nd Half 29 24 98 2 8 .140 .235 .221 .456
In May, as Basallo came into his own, he did what he always did in the minors – destroy fastballs. He hit .314 of fastballs that month and slugged .543. Since then, he is 15-for-100 against fastballs with just five extra base hits (all homers). That’s a massive red flag and I tend to think health and wear and tear have much to do with it. And probably some mounting frustration with one of MLB’s worst hitting staffs that has undermined many a fledgling career already.
Any chances of trying to end this season at anything close to the power and ferocity with which he was swinging the bat in midsummer is long gone. How much first base he ends up playing in the future – or even picking up some right field – remains to be seen. And hopefully he will not need any sort of procedures or clean ups this offseason.

item.title: [si.com] Aaron Judge’s Injury Hurts Yankees’ Playoff Hopes—but It Isn’t a Death Blow
item.dc:creator: Ryan Phillips
item.description: This is not the season Aaron Judge envisioned. The three-time American League MVP is on the injured list with a calf strain, and the Yankees got a deflating update Tuesday. Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain and has received a PPP injection to help speed healing. Manager Aaron Boone says the team is expecting him to miss the wild-card round of the playoffs. That’s a massive blow for a team that has stumbled down the stretch a bit. Judge missed 86 games earlier this season due to a rib inj
item.content:encoded:
This is not the season Aaron Judge envisioned.
The three-time American League MVP is on the injured list with a calf strain, and the Yankees got a deflating update Tuesday. Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain and has received a PPP injection to help speed healing. Manager Aaron Boone says the team is expecting him to miss the wild-card round of the playoffs.
That’s a massive blow for a team that has stumbled down the stretch a bit.
Judge missed 86 games earlier this season due to a rib injury. He finally returned to the lineup on Sept. 8 and, eight days later, left a game against the Twins after tweaking his calf during a swing. He went back on the IL on Sept. 18 and was eligible to come off as soon as Sunday. That is now unlikely, to say the least.
The 34-year-old has played in a full-season career-low 66 games this season and while pushing through the worst campaign of his career. Judge will end the regular season slashing .241/.360/.511, and his .871 OPS is the lowest he’s posted since a 27-game audition as a rookie in 2016. His wRC+ of 141 is his lowest since the COVID-shortened 2020 campaign.
He looked rusty when he came off the IL, and limped to a .513 OPS and a single home run in seven games.
It's been a lost season, but the Yankees have stayed afloat without him and entered Tuesday’s doubleheader with the Rays 89–66, with the top wild-card spot all but wrapped up. The team ranks 10th in runs scored and has leaned heavily on a pitching staff that boasts the best ERA in baseball at 3.22.
The Yankees are all but guaranteed to face the Red Sox in the opening round of the playoffs. Boston’s pitching staff ranks third in baseball with a 3.59 ERA, so runs figure to be at a premium in the series. The Red Sox won the season series, 7–6.
The list of Judge’s potential replacements in the lineup starts with Heliot Ramos, who has been manning right field, with Spencer Jones in center and Cody Bellinger in left. Ramos was added at the trade deadline and has struggled mightily to rack up hits in the Bronx. In 32 games with the team, he is slashing .172/.306/.366 with four home runs, 10 RBIs, 16 hits and a wRC+ of 91. He’s been bad, and he looks like the only option, as Trent Grisham appears far from returning. However, he has hit a home run in each of his last two games and is slashing .241/.305/.409 in September. That’s far from Judgian, but it’s at least some signs of life.
New York has gotten used to being without one of the best players on the planet for most of the season. The team deserves a lot of credit for getting this far, and can look to the 2021 Braves as inspiration in October—that Atlanta team lost Ronald Acuña Jr. for the season during the summer, entered the playoffs with just 88 wins and never faced elimination en route to a World Series title. And that Braves team didn’t have as talented of a pitching staff as these Yankees, who will also be granted a soft ALCS opponent with a worse record than them if they can advance that far.
With Judge down for the wild-card series, the Yankees will enter the playoffs on a down note no matter what happens over the season’s final week. But their biggest rival will still have to take down a plenty talented team in the hostile confines of Yankee Stadium—perhaps right after completing its season a day earlier. The injury gods may not be on the Yankees’ side right now, but if there’s one team the baseball gods have smiled upon throughout the sport’s existence, it’s them. Don’t count New York out yet.
Ryan Phillips is a senior writer on the Breaking and Trending News team at Sports Illustrated. He has worked in digital media since 2009, spending eight years at The Big Lead before joining SI in 2024. Phillips also co-hosts The Assembly Call Podcast about Indiana Hoosiers basketball and previously worked at Bleacher Report. He is a proud San Diego native and a graduate of Indiana University’s journalism program.
Follow rumorsandrants

item.content:encoded:
Texas Rangers shortstop Corey Seager has been a key driving force behind the team's playoff push as the 2026 season winds down.
With just one week to go in the regular season, all the Rangers' goals are still in front of them, but it hasn’t been the typical year for Seager.
Throughout much of the first half, Seager was on the Injured List, and when he was playing, he wasn’t lighting the world on fire by any means.
Corey Seager has looked better
Lately, that has been a much different story. Since July 31, Seager is hitting .293 with eight home runs and 22 RBIs in 44 games.
Additionally, Seager has been playing lights-out defense at shortstop, maintaining a perfect fielding percentage in that same span.
Entering the final week of the season, Texas holds a slight one-game lead in the American League West.
If the Rangers do wind up in the postseason field, it certainly won’t be a pretty picture that has gotten them there, but perhaps they know more than anyone: once you’re in, you’re in, and with Seager, they have one of the best postseason players in modern baseball history.
Rangers star knows about postseason play
Through 78 career postseason games, Seager has smashed 19 home runs and 48 RBI while amassing a pair of World Series MVP trophies.
A Seager-led-lineup in October could be dangerous for opposing pitching, but first, he has to help Texas get there.
There’s no doubt that with his current form, the Rangers feel good about where their offense stands heading into the critical final week.
On the other hand, the Texas pitching staff is starting to thin out, and they will need to have a couple of big performances from some of the guys they do have available if they want to keep their dreams of playing in October alive.
We know that the Rangers' pitching plans will pretty much remain TBD through the rest of the season, as manager Skip Schumaker has continued to describe the situation as “all-hands on deck”

item.description: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman, who suffered multiple facial fractures on the left side when he was struck by a foul ball while in the on-deck circle during Sunday's game, will not go on the injured list and in fact could return as soon as this coming weekend in Boston, manager Craig Counsell told reporters on Tuesday. item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman, who suffered multiple facial fractures on the left side when he was struck by a foul ball while in the on-deck circle during Sunday's game, will not go on the injured list and in fact could return as soon as this coming weekend in Boston, manager Craig Counsell told reporters on Tuesday.
"I think Alex is going to be fine," he said (via ESPN). "He's planning on playing."
The fluke injury occurred when Michael Busch hit a check swing foul ball Bregman's way in the fourth inning. Bregman simply did not have enough time to react given his proximity to home plate. He shared an update on social media Monday morning:
Alex Bregman shared another update to his IG story this morning of how his face is looking after getting hit with the foul ball yesterday:
[image or embed]
Other than pain tolerance, the biggest question is whether the swelling will subside soon enough so that Bregman can see out of his left eye. If his vision is impaired, he won't be able to play. There's pretty much no way around that. Given Counsell's comments on Tuesday, it seems like maybe the swelling reduction has made good progress.
Only six days remain in the regular season. In not placing Bregman on the injured list, it shows the Cubs are hopeful that, at a bare minimum, Bregman would be available for the Wild Card Series. Chicago is five games up on a wild-card spot and can clinch a postseason berth as early as Tuesday with a win over the Marlins or a loss by the Diamondbacks. They have been eliminated from the NL Central race.
As things stand headed into Tuesday's slate, the Cubs are lined up to face the Padres, though the NL wild-card race seeding is still up in the air.
If Bregman is unable to play in the Wild Card Series, some combination of Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramírez would likely fill in, though that certainly would be a downgrade. Instead, the Cubs would have to rely more heavily on National League MVP frontrunner Pete Crow-Armstrong, Seiya Suzuki, Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner and others.
Bregman, 32, is hitting .262/.352/.452 with 26 home runs this season. He has 19 homers in his last 61 games and has been Chicago's second-best player behind Crow-Armstrong. This is the first year of Bregman's five-year, $175 million contract with the Cubs.

item.title: [Fox News] Pirates ace Paul Skenes links concerning velocity dip to World Baseball Classic amid tough season
item.dc:creator: Ryan Canfield
item.description: The World Baseball Classic may have only been a couple of weeks long, but its impact was felt all season long. Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes has not been himself this year. His velocity has dipped, his command has been off, and after posting ERAs of 1.97 and 1.96, respectively, over the last two seasons, he has a 3.91 ERA this season. Why? Skenes said part of it was the World Baseball Classic. "There are a lot of other factors, so I don’t want to put everything on that," Skenes told the Pos
item.content:encoded:
The World Baseball Classic may have only been a couple of weeks long, but its impact was felt all season long.
Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes has not been himself this year. His velocity has dipped, his command has been off, and after posting ERAs of 1.97 and 1.96, respectively, over the last two seasons, he has a 3.91 ERA this season. Why? Skenes said part of it was the World Baseball Classic.
"There are a lot of other factors, so I don’t want to put everything on that," Skenes told the Post-Gazette. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit."
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
The World Baseball Classic ran from March 3 to March 17 this year, and Skenes said at that time of year, pitchers aren’t throwing at max effort.
"Usually, that time of year, you’re kind of ramping up and it’s a little bit slow. You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body," Skenes said. "One live (batting practice), you’re topping at 97 (mph), and then the next you’re 98, 99. And that wasn’t the case this year. ... Looking back, I don’t think that really helped."
Early in the season, Skenes pitched well despite not having his usual 98-mph fastball. In 2024, his rookie season, he averaged 98.8 mph, and last season he averaged 98.1 mph. This year, he is down to 96.8 mph.
Skenes didn’t have a set number for how hard he wanted to throw; he just wanted to throw harder. The 2025 NL Cy Young Award winner said he made mechanical adjustments to try to improve his velocity, but nothing came of them.
"Unfortunately, it’s probably going to take an offseason to get it back," Skenes said. "Yeah, it’s just tough."
Skenes didn’t blame all of his struggles on the World Baseball Classic, but he believed it had an impact. He also said he isn’t the only pitcher who was impacted.
"It definitely affected the year," Skenes said. "Unfortunately, I don’t think I’m the only one."
The Pirates hope their ace will have a strong offseason, return to form in 2027 and help the team make a postseason push, assuming there is a season amid the impending lockout.

item.title: [Fox News] El as de los Pirates, Paul Skenes, achaca la caída de su velocidad al Clásico Mundial de Béisbol, en medio de una temporada complicada
item.dc:creator: Ryan
item.content:encoded:
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
Puede que el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol solo durara un par de semanas, pero su impacto se notó durante toda la temporada.
Paul Skenes, el as de los Piratas de Pittsburgh, no ha estado a la altura este año. Su velocidad ha bajado, ha perdido precisión y, tras registrar unas medias de carreras limpias de 1,97 y 1,96, respectivamente, en las dos últimas temporadas, esta temporada tiene una media de 3,91. ¿Por qué? Skenes dijo que en parte se debía al Clásico Mundial de Béisbol.
«Hay un montón de factores más, así que no quiero achacárselo todo a eso», declaró Skenes al Post-Gazette. «Pero creo que, en cierto modo, esa fue un poco la raíz del asunto».
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
El Clásico Mundial de Béisbol se celebró este año del 3 al 17 de marzo, y Skenes dijo que, en esa época del año, los lanzadores no lanzan a toda su capacidad.
«Normalmente, en esa época del año, estás entrando en forma y todo va un poco lento. Puedes salir a la pista y ir encontrando tu ritmo», dijo Skenes. «En una sesión de bateo con lanzamientos reales, llegas a los 97 (mph), y en la siguiente ya vas a 98, 99. Pero este año no fue así... Mirando atrás, no creo que eso ayudara mucho».
Al principio de la temporada, Skenes lanzó bien a pesar de no tener su habitual bola rápida de 98 mph. En 2024, su temporada de novato, alcanzó una media de 98,8 mph, y la temporada pasada, una media de 98,1 mph. Este año, ha bajado a 96,8 mph.
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
Skenes no tenía una cifra concreta de a qué velocidad quería lanzar; simplemente quería lanzar más fuerte. El ganador del Premio Cy Young de la Liga Nacional de 2025 dijo que hizo algunos ajustes mecánicos para intentar mejorar su velocidad, pero no le sirvieron de nada.
«Por desgracia, probablemente me vaya a llevar toda la temporada baja recuperarme», dijo Skenes. «Sí, es duro».
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
Skenes no achacó todas sus dificultades al Clásico Mundial de Béisbol, pero creía que había influido. También dijo que no es el único lanzador al que le ha afectado.
«Sin duda, eso ha afectado al año», dijo Skenes. «Por desgracia, no creo que sea el único».
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
Los Pirates esperan que su as tenga una buena pretemporada, recupere su mejor nivel en 2027 y ayude al equipo a meterse en los playoffs, siempre y cuando haya temporada a pesar del cierre patronal que se avecina.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have officially named Chad Tracy as their full-time manager, removing the interim tag and signing him to a three-year contract. Tracy, who is 41 years old, took over the managerial role from Alex Cora on April 26 and has since led the team to a 74-55 record, securing an American League Wild Card berth.
Tracy's leadership has been instrumental in the team's success this season, and his appointment comes as the Red Sox continue to make bold moves under the guidance of Craig Breslow, the team's chief baseball officer. Breslow, known for his willingness to take significant in-season risks, has seen his strategies pay off with the team's second consecutive postseason appearance. On Tuesday (September 22), the Red Sox picked up Breslow's contract options for the 2029 and 2030 seasons, further solidifying his role in the organization.
Breslow's decision to fire Alex Cora and overhaul the coaching staff early in the season was a notable gamble that has since been vindicated. The Red Sox's aggressive approach included the mid-season acquisition of catcher Adley Rutschman and infielder Curtis Mead, moves that have contributed to the team's playoff run. According to the Boston Globe, Breslow emphasized the importance of acting decisively and creating a supportive environment for players to thrive.
As the Red Sox prepare for the postseason, Tracy expressed gratitude to his team, saying, "I want to express gratitude for everyone in the room. You stared impossible in the face. The position we were in, you beat it back and said, 'The hell with that, we’re going to the playoffs.'" His leadership and the team's resilience have set the stage for what fans hope will be a successful playoff run.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Matt Olson Has Been Waiting All Year for Another Chance at October
item.dc:creator: David Martinez
item.description: Matt Olson didn't need much time to explain why Sunday's division-clinching celebration felt different. For the Atlanta Braves first baseman, the moment was less about what Atlanta had accomplished and more about what the team had spent the previous six months trying to put behind it. "Sometimes you can take things for granted, and beating the playoffs so much last year left a sour taste in our mouth," Olson told Braves Vision's Wiley Ballard during the celebration. "I felt the focus from first
item.content:encoded:
Matt Olson didn't need much time to explain why Sunday's division-clinching celebration felt different.
For the Atlanta Braves first baseman, the moment was less about what Atlanta had accomplished and more about what the team had spent the previous six months trying to put behind it.
"Sometimes you can take things for granted, and beating the playoffs so much last year left a sour taste in our mouth," Olson told Braves Vision's Wiley Ballard during the celebration. "I felt the focus from first day of spring training."
That focus is what Olson kept coming back to after Atlanta swept the Astros to secure its first National League East title since 2023. The Braves have spent most of the season near the top of the division, but Olson said the urgency behind this group was noticeable from the beginning, particularly after missing out on last year's postseason.
Now, with the division secured and six regular-season games remaining, Olson finally gets to enjoy the part of the season he has been waiting for.
The difference is that Atlanta isn't simply arriving in October after a comfortable regular season. Olson believes the Braves have spent the last few months getting ready for what comes next.
"We've been playing playoff baseball for the last couple months," Olson told Ballard. "Just the teams we're matching up against and the arms, which is good because you build some scars, you get battle-tested a little bit, and you get prepared."
That comment says plenty about how Olson is viewing the final stretch.
The Braves have spent the season facing playoff-caliber teams and pitchers, and Olson believes those games have given Atlanta something that can't really be replicated during a lighter part of the schedule. The goal now isn't to prove they can handle that environment. They've already spent months doing it.
That belief also connects back to the influence of first-year manager Walt Weiss.
Olson called Weiss "probably our No. 1 person" when discussing the focus Atlanta established during spring training. Weiss encouraged the Braves to play with aggression from the beginning, and Olson said he felt that message throughout the season.
There were obviously difficult stretches along the way, but Olson noticed something that continued to separate this team.
"We had a couple bad series, we go to a big series and we rise up to the occasion," Olson told Ballard.
That became particularly important as Atlanta dealt with the expectations that come with trying to win the division again. Instead of allowing every rough stretch to linger, the Braves repeatedly found ways to respond.
Now they have a division title to show for it.
Olson has done his part offensively, hitting .253 with a .506 slugging percentage, 40 home runs and a 123 wRC+ while earning his fourth career All-Star selection. But the regular-season numbers aren't what seem to be driving his excitement right now.
He's thinking about October.
Last year's disappointment is still sitting somewhere in the back of Olson's mind. This time, though, he believes the Braves have spent enough of the season preparing for what awaits them.
And after waiting all year for another chance, Olson finally has his.

item.title: [heavy.com] Braves Announce Matt Olson Move Before Reds Series
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: The Atlanta Braves have clinched a spot in the playoffs, winning the National League East division this year. But Atlanta is looking for a little more than just that as the postseason gets going next week. Atlanta is still in the running for a top-two seed in the NL, but they find themselves sitting four games back as the last week of the regular season gets going. Atlanta is coming off a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros, giving themselves some confidence coming into the final week. But th
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves have clinched a spot in the playoffs, winning the National League East division this year.
But Atlanta is looking for a little more than just that as the postseason gets going next week. Atlanta is still in the running for a top-two seed in the NL, but they find themselves sitting four games back as the last week of the regular season gets going.
Atlanta is coming off a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros, giving themselves some confidence coming into the final week. But this team has some work to do to prepare for the playoffs.
The Braves will now be opening up a three-game series against the Cincinnati Reds this week, starting today. This will be the final home series for Atlanta during the regular season, and the team will be looking to stack some wins before the playoffs begin.
Atlanta has a chance to take advantage of playing the Reds, whose pitching has been poor this season. But the Braves will need to take care of business, while getting some help to avoid playing in the wild-card series next week.
Matt Olson Decision Announced by Braves
Ahead of the series opener with the Reds, the Braves have announced the lineup for the contest. Within the lineup, slugger Matt Olson will be hitting third for Atlanta, playing at first base.
Braves 9/22
R. Acuña Jr. RF
D. Baldwin DH
M. Olson 1B
O. Albies 2B
M. Harris II CF
M. Dubón LF
A. Riley 3B
S. Murphy C
H. Kim SS
J. Ritchie SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 22, 2026
Olson has been great for Atlanta this year, hitting .253 with 40 home runs and 89 RBIs, while posting an OPS of .830. His consistency in the lineup has allowed the Braves to be one of the stronger offenses in all of baseball.
Walt Weiss Leading the Charge For Braves
One reason for the Braves’ success this season has been the leadership from manager Walt Weiss. Atlanta has leaned on Weiss to navigate the long year, and it has resulted in a massive turnaround for this clubhouse.
“When I look back on it, it was too much,” Weiss said. “That’s a big part of this job is having good timing for those conversations, whether it’s individually or collectively with your group. Your timing has to be good, or the message isn’t going to hit the same.”
Multiple players have spoken highly of Weiss this year, and how he has navigated everything. Braves ace Chris Sale gave some high praise to the manager after the team clinched the NL East crown.
“(With Walt) it’s like coaching down a highway and not coaching down a hallway,” Sale said. “ He lets you get here, but it’s not a correction at every turn. If you’re getting corrected going down a hallway, it’s this, it’s that. But down the highway, you get a little bit more leniency.”
The Braves will continue to lean on Weiss’s leadership throughout the playoffs, hoping for another run at a World Series title. But for now, the focus will be on the Reds series, with the Braves trying to get hot entering the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
A falta de una semana para que termine la temporada regular en la MLB, el panorama de playoffs comienza a definirse y con ello te presentamos aquellos peloteros mexicanos que ya aseguraron su clasificación a playoffs y quienes todavía están en la pelea por entrar a la postemporada.
Mexicanos que ya aseguraron su pase a postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos en las últimas ediciones de los playoffs ha sido constante y este año no será la excepción pues hasta ahorita se tiene confirmada la participación de cuatro peloteros mexicanos y dos con estatus todavía pendiente, ya que uno está en sucursales y el otro se encuentra en lista de lesionados.
PUBLICIDAD
A continuación, te presentamos la lista de jugadores nacionales que estarán en los playoffs:
Jonathan Aranda (Tampa Bay Rays)
Ha firmado su campaña más sólida y consagratoria en MLB. Con 149 juegos jugados, el infielder presume un promedio de bateo de .277, conectando 156 imparables, 22 cuadrangulares y remolcando 92 carreras, convirtiéndose en una pieza medular en el lineup de los Rays.
Jarren Durán (Boston Red Sox):
Se ha consolidado como un auténtico motor en los senderos y el jardín central. A lo largo de la temporada suma 20 jonrones, 69 carreras impulsadas y 19 bases robadas en 145 encuentros, destacando además por su velocidad con 5 triples.
PUBLICIDAD
Joey Ortiz (Milwaukee Brewers):
Ha sido una de las grandes revelaciones del año tras su llegada a Milwaukee, aportando una defensa de élite en el cuadro y un bateo sumamente oportuno que ayudó a los Brewers a amarrar temprano su boleto a octubre.
Patrick Sandoval (Boston Red Sox):
El lanzador que representó a México en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol regresó esta temporada tras un periodo largo fuera de las canchas y ha tenido altibajos con los Boston Red Sox con una efectividad de 5.15 y un récord de 1-7.
Manuel Rodríguez (Tampa Bay Rays):
El lanzador yucateco venía sumando valiosos relevos con efectividad de 3.86 y 8 ponches en el bullpen de Tampa Bay en los cuatro juegos que disputó.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, Manuel Rodríguez se encuentra actualmente en la lista de lesionados (IL) de 15 días debido a una distensión en la espalda baja (low back strain), por lo que el cuerpo técnico espera su evolución para ver si podrá estar listo en las primeras rondas de los playoffs.
Alek Thomas (Oklahoma City Comets):
Después de haber sido cambiado desde los Arizona Diamondbacks a inicios de año, el jardinero Alek Thomas se encuentra actualmente en las sucursales de Los Angeles Dodgers
Aunque tuvo una breve participación de 7 juegos con el primer equipo de los Dodgers bateando para .211, la tremenda profundidad del roster angelino ha hecho que se mantenga buscando ritmo en el sistema de ligas menores, a la espera de un llamado que lo devuelva al roster de postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
Peloteros mexicanos todavía buscan entrar a la postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos aumentará conforme avance la semana, con varios representantes en equipos que continúan en competencia por buscar entrar a los playoffs.
Toronto Blue Jays cuenta con Alejandro Kirk, Tibo Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Luis Urías. Por su parte, Randy Arozarena y Andrés Muñoz forman parte de los Seattle Mariners.
Isaac Paredes representa a los Houston Astros, mientras Javier Assad se encuentra con los Chicago Cubs. Alejandro Osuna integra el roster de los Texas Rangers.
Taijuan Walker juega con los Philadelphia Phillies y Jeremiah Estrada pertenece a los San Diego Padres.
Cada uno luchará hasta el último segundo por entrar a la postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Riley Greene Gets Blunt About Tigers Missing the Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Glenn Kaplan
item.description: The Detroit Tigers were officially eliminated from playoff contention on Sunday, and Riley Greene did not dress up what that feels like. With five games left in the season, Detroit sits at 74-83, third place in the American League Central, and will watch October from home. The Tigers were in the playoffs in 2024 and in 2025, and Greene was a part of both of those teams. Detroit did not do enough this season to contend. There will be a lot of questions about this franchise as the offseason approa
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Tigers were officially eliminated from playoff contention on Sunday, and Riley Greene did not dress up what that feels like. With five games left in the season, Detroit sits at 74-83, third place in the American League Central, and will watch October from home.
The Tigers were in the playoffs in 2024 and in 2025, and Greene was a part of both of those teams. Detroit did not do enough this season to contend. There will be a lot of questions about this franchise as the offseason approaches.
Riley Greene Does Not Sugarcoat the Tigers Missing the Playoffs
On Monday, Greene talked about the season with Brad Galli of the Brad Galli Show. The star outfielder said:
"Yeah, it sucks. We've been there the past two years, and our goal is to win the World Series, and we came up short."
One of the biggest issues with the Tigers this season was injuries. Greene also added:
"It's been tough. Of course, there's gonna be injuries and things are gonna happen, but at the end of the day, we didn't win enough baseball games."
One of the biggest injuries on the Tigers roster this season was Javier Baez, who split time between shortstop and center field. He hurt his right ankle on April 28 against the Atlanta Braves, trying to avoid a tag on the way to first base. The high-ankle sprain never let go, and Detroit moved him to the 60-day injured list on June 11. He will have only one year remaining on his contract once the 2026 MLB season comes to an end.
Riley Greene Had a Solid Season Despite Missing the Playoffs
Despite missing the playoffs, it was another solid season for the Tigers outfielder. Greene was an American League All-Star for the third straight year, this time as a starter. So far this season, he has appeared in 136 games. Greene has a .284 batting average with 21 home runs and 75 RBIs, along with three stolen bases on four attempts. His on-base percentage is .371, his slugging percentage is .481, and his OPS is .852.
Detroit's Problems Are Bigger Than Riley Greene
Greene will be under team control for two more seasons and cannot reach free agency until 2029. The Tigers settled with him on a one-year, $5 million deal in January to avoid arbitration, and at some point they will need to give the 25-year-old a long-term contract extension. He is not the problem on this team. Detroit has other issues to address this offseason.

item.title: [marca usa] La grave lesión de Alex Bregman podría obligar a la MLB a romper una tradición de larga data: "No tenemos por qué seguir haciendo eso"
item.dc:creator: Matias Wodner
item.description: - MLB. Gran preocupación por Aaron Judge: “Existe una fuerte posibilidad de que no vuelva a jugar esta temporada” - MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie” En este momento, los Chicago Cubs necesitan que todos aporten al máximo para el tramo final de la temporada regular. El título de la división está fuera de alcance, pero el primer puesto en la carrera por el comodín de la Liga Nacional sigue en juego. Lamentablemente, el equipo p
item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Gran preocupación por Aaron Judge: “Existe una fuerte posibilidad de que no vuelva a jugar esta temporada”
- MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”
En este momento, los Chicago Cubs necesitan que todos aporten al máximo para el tramo final de la temporada regular. El título de la división está fuera de alcance, pero el primer puesto en la carrera por el comodín de la Liga Nacional sigue en juego. Lamentablemente, el equipo perdió a uno de sus mejores jugadores para esta recta final el pasado fin de semana.
Alex Bregman sufrió una lesión terrible, y ocurrió de la manera más desafortunada posible. Mientras esperaba su turno en el círculo de espera (*on-deck circle*), Bregman recibió un golpe en la cara por una bola de foul bateada por un compañero de equipo. Sufrió múltiples fracturas faciales, y la imagen que se vio tras el incidente fue impactante.
La lesión de Bregman ha llevado a muchos aficionados a plantearse un par de cosas. En primer lugar, a muchos les sorprende que este tipo de incidentes no ocurran con más frecuencia. El margen de error es mínimo cuando los bateadores que esperan su turno se colocan tan cerca de la caja de bateo. Hemos visto situaciones similares antes, pero resulta algo sorprendente que no sean más habituales.
Trevor Plouffe pide a la MLB que proteja a los bateadores que esperan su turno en el futuro
Sin embargo, aunque no suceda tan a menudo como cabría suponer, incluso exjugadores de la MLB como Trevor Plouffe creen que ha llegado el momento de que el béisbol implemente cambios para evitar este tipo de lesiones en el futuro. Plouffe expresó su opinión el lunes en el podcast "Talkin’ Baseball".
"Hace falta que ocurra algo así. Por ejemplo, si esto hubiera pasado en los playoffs y, de repente, Alex Bregman ya no pudiera jugar, eso sacudiría a la gente y provocaría una reacción. Quizás esto ya sea lo suficientemente grave. ¿Qué tal si ponemos una red protectora o algo parecido?"
Simplemente no hay razón para que un jugador esté tan cerca cuando no está bateando activamente. Es cierto que estar tan cerca permite al bateador que espera su turno conocer mejor al lanzador que está en el montículo, pero eso también pueden hacerlo desde el dugout o contando con mayor protección a su alrededor.

item.content:encoded:
The Mariners can hope that Randy Arozarena stays. But they also know they need to prepare for what their 2027 lineup looks like without him. He has easily become one of the hardest bats to replace.
Seattle Times beat reporter Ryan Divish brought that problem into focus on Foul Territory. He expects Arozarena to prefer the East Coast and guessed Boston could be ready to pay him handsomely. It’s just a prediction. The Red Sox haven’t announced any kind of serious interest. Regardless of where he goes, the Mariners need to be prepared.
Randy Arozarena’s 2026 Surge Raises the Stakes for the Mariners
His first 54 games after the 2024 trade were uninspiring. He posted a .231 average, five home runs and a .733 OPS. In his first full Mariners season, he hit only .238, but supplied 27 homers and 31 steals. He kept producing even when the hits were harder to find.
This year, the whole line has changed. Entering Sept. 22, Arozarena is slashing .279/.376/.481 with 26 homers, 106 runs, 23 steals and an .857 OPS. Compared with 2025, his average is up 41 points, his OBP 42 points and his slugging 55 points. He has nearly matched last year’s career high in homers while reaching base more often.
Now put that beside Seattle’s .232/.312/.380 team batting line. Arozarena is 64 points ahead in OBP and 101 points ahead in slugging. If he walks, the Mariners lose a right-handed bat who gets aboard, hits for power and still runs.
What Arozarena Has Done at Fenway Park
Boston is easy to picture because Arozarena has already hit well at Fenway. In 32 career games there, he’s slashed .278/.351/.481 with five home runs and 19 RBI with a 135 wRC+ in those games, meaning his offense has been 35 percent above league average after adjusting for park. He also homered in consecutive games there during Seattle’s visit at the turn of September.
Thirty-two games cannot tell us what he would do over a full season with the Red Sox. The numbers do tell us he can handle that setting. His .481 career slugging percentage at Fenway even matches his .481 mark across this entire season. There’s no reason to sell a home run surge. But we can see the potential. Arozarena can turn on a pitch and drive it toward the Green Monster, where hard contact can become a double off the wall or a ball can fly over it. He has spent half his games trying to produce at T-Mobile Park. Fenway would be a much friendlier setting for half of his games. Also, being in the same division with the Yankees stadium could also help pile his stats.
The East Coast idea has a personal thread, too. Arozarena became a star with Tampa Bay and spent his last night as a Ray among the fans in Randy Land. We can wonder whether the Rays ever explore a reunion.
The Mariners should make Arozarena a serious offer. His age and below-average outfield grades give them a reason to be careful about the number of years. Divish doubts Seattle will chase Boston through a bidding war, and we understand why the club would set a limit. We will judge that limit alongside the plan for the lineup it leaves behind.
If Arozarena signs elsewhere, Seattle needs another proven bat and a credible answer in left field. The club should know which young players can compete for the job and what production it still has to acquire. Planning for life without Randy starts with admitting exactly how much Randy has given the Mariners.
Tremayne Person is the Publisher for Mariners On SI and the Site Expert at Friars on Base, with additional bylines across FanSided’s MLB division. He founded the Keep It Electric podcast in 2023 and covers baseball with a blend of analysis, context, and a little well-timed side-eye just to keep things honest. Tremayne grew up a Mariners fan in Richmond, Va., and that passion ultimately led him to move to Seattle to cover the team closely and become a regular at home games. Through his writing, he connects with fans who want a deeper, more personal understanding of the game. When he’s not at T-Mobile Park, he’s with his dog, gaming, or finding the next storyline worth digging into.
Follow TremaynePerson

On Tuesday, the Philadelphia Phillies will open up a series with the Milwaukee Brewers (at home).
They had the day off on Monday following a four-game series with the New York Mets at Citi Field.
The Phillies split four games with the Mets (and most recently won by a score of 7-2 on Sunday).
Cristopher Sanchez got the start.
He allowed just two earned runs in 6.1 innings.
Phillies Star Cristopher Sanchez Sends Out 13-Word Post
Ahead of Tuesday’s series with the Brewers, Sanchez sent out a post to Instagram.
He wrote: “Different stadiums, different uniforms, same focus and the same plan: contribute to winning 🔥❤️”
There were over 10,000 likes on his post in less than 24 hours.
Looking At Sanchez
Sanchez is in the middle of his 6th season at the MLB level (all with the Phillies).
He is a two-time MLB All-Star.
Right now, the 29-year-old is 18-6 with a 2.93 ERA in 32 starts.
Looking At The Phillies Right Now
The Phillies are the second-place team in the National League East with an 86-70 record in 156 games.
They have gone 4-6 over their last ten games (and are 41-34 in 75 games at home).
Following the Brewers, the Phillies will play their final series of the 2026 regular season when they host the Tampa Bay Rays.
Scott Lauber of The Philadelphia Inquirer wrote (on Monday): “Brewers-Phillies pitching matchups: Tuesday- RHP Dustin May (7-9, 4.61) vs. RHP Zack Wheeler (13-5, 2.99) Wednesday- RHP Logan Henderson (10-3, 2.51) vs. RHP Aaron Nola (7-10, 4.49) Thursday- TBD vs. TBD”
Looking At The Brewers Right Now
The Brewers are the top team in the National League Central with a 98-58 record in 156 games.
They have gone 8-2 over their last ten games (and are 46-32 in 78 games on the road).
Following the Phillies, the Brewers will finish the regular season (at home) when they host the St. Louis Cardinals.
